output.overall_assessment: The auditor's finding is accurate and well-evidenced. Independent re-reading confirms: (a) `/api/integration/:integrationID` is NOT registered in `apps/server/src/routes.rs` — only the TODO comment at `routes.rs:898` references it; (b) the handler `integration::get` exists at `apps/server/src/handlers/integration.rs:193-201` and is fully implemented but unreachable via HTTP; (c) clients sending `GET /api/integration/foo` get 404 from axum's router (no matching route). Severity `critical` is correct. The `not_implemented` conformance classification is correct. Forward-looking schema analysis (if the route WERE wired): the handler at `integration.rs:193-201` would return `Location.response(IntegrationInfo)` for known IDs, where `IntegrationInfo` (defined at `integration.rs:65-71`) has `{id: String, name: String, methods: Vec<Value>, connections: Vec<Value>}`. Schema check: `id` matches `Integration.ID` (no brand constraint at wire level); `name` is `Schema.String` ✓; `methods: Vec<Value>` is always empty (build_catalog sets `methods: vec![]`) but `Schema.Array(Method)` accepts empty ✓; `connections: Vec<Value>` populated with `{type: "credential", id, label}` (matches contract's `Connection.CredentialInfo` variant at `schema/connection.ts:7-11` ✓). For unknown IDs, the handler returns `{location}` only — no `data` field — correctly implementing `UndefinedOr(Integration.Info)` ✓. Brand constraints: `Integration.ID` has no `isStartsWith` check (`schema/integration.ts:11`), so Loom's plain `String` is conformant. Tag/union handling: `Connection.Info` is a tagged union by `type` with two variants (`CredentialInfo`, `EnvInfo`); Loom only emits `CredentialInfo` (`EnvInfo` variant is unrepresented because no env-based integrations exist, but the union type itself is well-formed). If wired, the endpoint would be largely schema-conformant. The blocker is purely route registration. No new schema deviations to add — schema analysis is moot when the endpoint is non-functional.

Only `integration.list` is wired (via `bootstrap::get_api_integrations` returning empty array at `bootstrap.rs:260-265`, not the real `integration::list` handler). The handler `integration::get` exists at `apps/server/src/handlers/integration.rs:193-201` and is fully implemented with proper `UndefinedOr` semantics (returns `{location}` only when the id is unknown), but it's unreachable via HTTP. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/routes.rs:318-321` confirms the route is wired to `handlers::health::get_permission_saved`. deviations.contract_says: Contract requires success: Schema.Struct({ data: Schema.Record(Session.ID, SessionActive) }) where SessionActive = { type: Schema.Literal(\"running\") }. The response body MUST be { data: { \"ses_xxx\": { type: \"running\" }, \"ses_yyy\": { type: \"running\" } } } — a Record (Map) keyed by SessionID with a single discriminator field. Missing keys = inactive sessions.
deviations.loom_does: Handler at v2_compat.rs:87-103 returns { sessions: [{ id, state: \"busy\"|\"idle\", modelID, providerID, agent, startedAt, updatedAt }, ...] } — a JSON array of rich session objects wrapped in a {sessions: [...]} object (NOT {data: [...]}). The state field uses Loom's own two-value enum (busy/idle) not the contract's single value (running).
deviations.evidence_contract: packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:146-155 (HttpApiEndpoint.get with success: Schema.Struct({ data: Schema.Record(Session.ID, SessionActive) }))
deviations.impact: HIGH: clients conforming to the contract will fail to parse the response entirely. (1) They expect response.data to be a Map/Record, but Loom returns response.sessions as an array. (2) They expect Map values to be { type: \"running\" } sentinels, but Loom returns rich objects with state field. (3) They interpret absent Map keys as inactive, but Loom's array has all sessions (active + idle). The endpoint is fundamentally non-conformant — the wire-level shape is incompatible.

output.notes: Conformance level: NON_CONFORMANT. The handler is located in v2_compat.rs (the project's v1-compat layer) and was likely designed for OpenChamber TUI or v1 clients. It returns the WRONG response shape for v2 SDK clients. The fix would be: (1) change field name `sessions` → `data`, (2) change array → Map keyed by session.id, (3) change value shape from rich object → { type: \"running\" } sentinel. The richer Loom data (modelID, providerID, agent, startedAt, updatedAt) could either be discarded or exposed as an additional endpoint (e.g. /api/session/list). output.overall_assessment: Auditor correctly identified that `agent.list` is a hardcoded stub (DEV-3) — this is the dominant issue and should be classified HIGH not medium, because the endpoint fails its core contract purpose: "Retrieve currently registered agents." Re-verifying the other findings from a behavior angle, DEV-1 is REJECTED (the missing fields are optional per Effect schema `optional()` semantics, which drop on encode) and DEV-2 is REJECTED (the `locationQueryOpenApi` annotation is OpenAPI documentation only and has zero runtime effect — Loom parses query params via the `LocationQuery` extractor regardless). I add three new high-severity findings the auditor missed: polling cannot detect config changes (NEW-1), `mode: "primary"` does not reflect actual runtime dispatch (NEW-2), and `permissions: []` does not match the actual runtime permission store (NEW-3) — all instances of the broader pattern that the endpoint publishes metadata the runtime does not honor, creating a confused-deputy risk for clients building UIs against it.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: Effect schema `optional()` helper drops fields on encode. `model`, `system`, `color`, `steps` are all marked `.pipe(optional)` in schema/agent.ts:22,24,28,29. Their absence from the response is the canonical serialization, not a deviation. `description` is also optional but is included — both forms (present or absent) are schema-valid. The auditor's framing "missing optional fields" is technically true but conflates "absent" with "violation" — for optional fields, absent is the default conformant state. The auditor themselves noted "impact is minimal" — this is because there is no violation to begin with.

`.annotateMerge(locationQueryOpenApi)` is an OpenAPI documentation annotation only — it tells the Effect HTTP API to emit `style: deepObject, explode: true` in the generated OpenAPI spec for the `location` query param. Loom is an axum server that does not generate OpenAPI specs from these annotations; runtime query parsing is handled by the `LocationQuery` extractor (location.rs:88-93) which uses serde rename to handle the bracketed form `location[directory]=..` directly. With or without the annotation, the runtime parses the query identically. From a behavior angle, this deviation has zero observable effect — the route accepts the deepObject query correctly.

output.notes: POST /api/session/:sessionID/revert/commit is registered, returns 204 NoContent on success (matching HttpApiSchema.NoContent), and returns SessionNotFoundError (404 with branded JSON body) when the session does not exist. Route path and HTTP method match the contract exactly, handler is real (not v2_compat), and global auth middleware is applied. The happy path is fully conformant. The contract declares only SessionNotFoundError as the error class for this endpoint, but the Loom handler emits two additional undeclared error responses (409 with bare text "no revert is staged" when no revert is staged, 404 with bare text "revert message not found" when the staged messageID is no longer in the timeline) that use plain text bodies instead of any contract-shaped error schema. Side effects are correct: state.messages/parts are drained after the boundary, persist_messages is called, and the session.next.revert.committed event with payload { timestamp, sessionID, messageID } is published (matches RevertEvent.Committed schema).

side_effects.notes: On success: (1) drains messages after the staged messageID boundary from state.messages, (2) cascade-deletes the corresponding entries from state.parts, (3) calls persist_messages to durably save the new message list, (4) publishes a durable session.next.revert.committed event with payload { timestamp, sessionID, messageID } — matches RevertEvent.Committed schema exactly (session-event.ts:441-445). Idempotency: not idempotent — calling revert/commit consumes the staged entry via .remove() and drains messages; a second call returns 409. State mutations are not strictly atomic across messages + parts locks (two separate write locks), but no data inconsistency is observable since the partial state is consistent.

The auditor's most severe finding (DEV-1 critical) is a FALSE POSITIVE — the auditor missed the `#[serde(rename = "type")]` attribute at `fs.rs:102` and concluded that Loom serializes the field as `"kind"`. In fact, the Rust struct field is named `kind` (because `type` is a Rust reserved keyword and requires `r#type` to use as a field name) but the serde rename attribute ensures the wire JSON field is `"type"`. The wire output is `{ "path": "...", "type": "file" | "directory" }` — fully conformant with the contract's `FileSystem.Entry`. This invalidates the entire `non_conformant` classification. Likewise, DEV-3 (ListQuery has a `kind` field) is a false positive — the auditor confused `ListQuery` (fs.list, no `type` field per contract fs.ts:8-11) with `FindQuery` (fs.find, has `type` field per fs.ts:13-18). Re-read of `fs.rs:170-176` confirms Loom's `ListQuery` has only `location` (flattened) and `path` — exactly matching the contract. DEV-4 (missing `locationQueryOpenApi` annotation) is confirmed but severity `low` is correct. DEV-2 (generic error shape) is technically valid but the contract declares NO error classes for fs.list — so the deviation is server-wide convention consistency, not an endpoint-specific contract violation. Conformance level should be `partial`, not `non_conformant`.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: REJECTED — FALSE POSITIVE. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:99-104` carefully. The struct is `struct FsEntry<'a> { path: String, #[serde(rename = "type")] kind: &'a str }`. The `#[serde(rename = "type")]` attribute at `fs.rs:102` instructs serde to serialize the Rust field `kind` under the JSON key `"type"`. The Rust field is named `kind` (not `type`) because `type` is a Rust reserved keyword — using it as a field name would require the `r#type` raw identifier. The serde rename is the idiomatic, correct solution. Wire output is `{"path": "...", "type": "file" | "directory"}`, which matches the contract's `FileSystem.Entry = Schema.Struct({ path: RelativePath, type: Schema.Literals([\"file\", \"directory\"]) })` (filesystem.ts:14-18) EXACTLY. The auditor's claim that Loom \"serializes as { path, kind: \\\"file\\\" }\" is factually wrong — they missed the serde rename attribute. Severity `critical` is incorrect; this is not a deviation at all. The handler's doc-comment at `fs.rs:97-98` even explicitly states `FileSystem.Entry = { path: RelativePath, type: \"file\" | \"directory\" }` to document the wire shape, confirming the developer was aware of the contract requirement.

PARTIALLY CONFIRMED but severity is overstated. Re-read `packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:35-48` — the `fs.list` endpoint declares NO `error: [...]` field. The contract's success schema is `Location.response(Schema.Array(FileSystem.Entry))` with no error annotation. So Loom's generic `{error: \"...\"}` shape does not violate any declared contract error class. However, the server-wide convention (`packages/protocol/src/errors.ts:3-11` and similar for `SessionNotFoundError`, etc.) defines `InvalidRequestError` with body `{message, kind?, field?}` — and other endpoints in the codebase do emit this shape. So Loom's generic string error is a server-wide consistency gap, not an endpoint-specific contract violation. The 403 path traversal and 500 I/O errors are not declared in the contract either — they're implementation choices (path traversal check + I/O mapping). Severity `high` is too high; should be `medium` (server-wide convention gap) or `low` (no contract violation). Body shape `{error: \"<io error message>\"}` doesn't conform to any contract error class shape, but no class is declared, so this is convention drift, not contract violation.

REJECTED — FALSE POSITIVE. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:170-176` carefully: `pub struct ListQuery { #[serde(flatten)] pub location: LocationQuery, #[serde(default)] pub path: Option<String> }`. There is NO `kind` field in Loom's `ListQuery`. The contract's `ListQuery` at `fs.ts:8-11` is `Schema.Struct({...LocationQuery.fields, path: RelativePath.pipe(Schema.optional)})` — also has no `type` field. The auditor confused `ListQuery` (used by `fs.list`) with `FindQuery` (used by `fs.find`, which DOES have `type: FileSystem.FindInput.fields.type` at `fs.ts:16`). The `type` query field is on `FindQuery`, not `ListQuery`. Loom's `ListQuery` correctly mirrors the contract — only `location` and `path`. The citation `apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:436` is wrong — `fs.rs:436` is not a `ListQuery` struct definition; it's likely from `find_query` or a different struct. The auditor appears to have copy-pasted the fs.find audit notes into fs.list. No deviation exists.

new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `session.rs:1329`: `let _ = publish_durable(&state, \"session.next.revert.cleared\", ...)` — the result of `publish_durable` is discarded with `let _`. If the durable store fails, no error is reported to the client.

new_deviations_found.title: TOCTOU race: session could be deleted between 404 check and clear
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on race conditions.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `session.rs:1325-1328` acquires `state.sessions.read()` for the 404 check, releases the lock, then acquires `state.staged_reverts.write()` for the removal. Between these two operations, the session could be deleted via `delete_session`. The handler would have already passed the 404 check, then `state.staged_reverts.write().remove(...)` would still succeed even though the session no longer exists.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior: orphaned `staged_reverts` entries could remain if a session is deleted between clear attempts. Severity `low` (no security issue, just a minor inconsistency). The orphan would be cleaned up if a new session with the same id is created (it would inherit the stale staged_revert).
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:1325-1328 (separate locks for sessions read and staged_reverts write).

new_deviations_found.title: SSE event emitted even when nothing was actually cleared
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on event semantics.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `session.rs:1328-1336` calls `state.staged_reverts.write().remove(...)` (returns `Option<Value>`, discarded) then publishes the event. The event fires regardless of whether the entry existed.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior: subscribers receive `session.next.revert.cleared` events even when nothing was actually cleared (e.g., the session had no staged revert). Severity `low` (defensive design — no harm but extra events).

new_deviations_found.title: `UnknownError` (500) never produced on internal failures
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: [SessionNotFoundError, UnknownError]` (`session.ts:275`). `UnknownError` should map to 500 on unexpected errors.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler has no try/except. Any serialization error or internal failure returns whatever default axum produces (probably 500 with plain text) rather than the contract's `{_tag: \"UnknownError\", message, ref?}` shape.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior gap: 500 errors don't match the contract's `UnknownError` body shape. Severity `low`.

deviations.title: Response shape: Loom returns bare SessionInfo, contract requires { data: Session.Info } envelope
deviations.contract_says: Contract requires `success: Schema.Struct({ data: Session.Info })` — body shape is { data: Session.Info } with Session.Info containing id, parentID, projectID, agent, model, cost, tokens, time, title, location, subpath, revert?.
deviations.loom_does: Handler at session.rs:56-62 returns `Json(serde_json::to_value(s).unwrap_or(Value::Null))` which serializes the internal SessionInfo struct DIRECTLY. There is no `{ data: ... }` envelope — clients receive the SessionInfo fields at the root of the response.
deviations.impact: MEDIUM: clients conforming to the contract will fail to parse the response. The contract's { data: ... } envelope is standard for session-scoped endpoints (per the pattern seen in session.context, session.history, session.active, session.messages, session.message — all of which return bare { data: ... } envelopes, not Location.response). The internal SessionInfo fields may or may not match Session.Info contract shape — the to_value serialization may produce the correct fields, but the lack of envelope means even a perfect Session.Info projection will fail contract-conforming clients.

deviations.title: 404 response has no body; SessionNotFoundError class shape not returned
deviations.contract_says: Contract declares error: [SessionNotFoundError(404)] with shape { sessionID: Schema.String, message: Schema.String } and name: Schema.Literal("SessionNotFoundError").
deviations.loom_does: Handler at session.rs:60 returns `StatusCode::NOT_FOUND.into_response()` — empty body, no SessionNotFoundError class.
deviations.impact: MEDIUM: 404 status is correct, but the body is empty. Clients conforming to the contract will try to parse a SessionNotFoundError body and fail (or treat as generic 404). Severity medium because (a) the 404 status allows clients to detect the error at HTTP level, (b) no client-visible information leak (no sessionID echoed), but (c) the contract's error class is structurally missing. This is the same pattern as other session.* endpoints in Loom (e.g. session.history, session.context) which use 404 with empty body rather than the contract's SessionNotFoundError shape.

missing_features: SessionNotFoundError class shape (Loom returns empty 404 body)
{ data: ... } envelope wrapping (Loom returns bare SessionInfo)
Session.ID brand validation on path param (Loom accepts any string)
extra_features: None (defensive implementation)
output.notes: Conformance level: PARTIAL. Two medium deviations: response shape (bare vs wrapped) and 404 body (empty vs SessionNotFoundError). The route IS registered and the handler is real — not the case for the other W2 endpoints. The bare-response pattern matches other session.* endpoints in Loom (session.history, session.context, session.message all do the same), suggesting a project-wide convention that diverges from the contract. The internal SessionInfo struct's fields may or may not match Session.Info exactly — the handler uses `serde_json::to_value(s)` which serializes whatever fields the internal struct has, so if SessionInfo has extra fields (e.g. internal-only flags), those would leak into the response. This is a broader concern: the audit is on a "session.*-style bare response" pattern that Loom consistently uses, but the contract's expectation is a structured { data: ... } envelope. To be fully conformant, the handler would need to (1) wrap the SessionInfo in { data: ... } envelope, (2) project the internal struct to match the contract's Session.Info fields exactly, (3) return SessionNotFoundError body for 404. None of this is currently implemented. The endpoint is operational for Loom's internal use (TUI inspecting sessions) but does not match the contract exactly.

new_deviations_found.title: Forward-looking: `query.cursor` is parsed but never read — pagination is broken
new_deviations_found.contract_says: query: SessionMessagesQuery (message.ts:7-22) with cursor: Schema.optional(Schema.String). cursor annotation: \"Opaque pagination cursor returned as cursor.previous or cursor.next in the previous response.\" The contract expects the server to honor the cursor to advance through pages.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: The handler at messages.rs:119-177 extracts `Query(query): Query<SessionMessagesQuery>` (line 122) but the cursor field is NEVER referenced in the handler body. The handler always starts from the beginning of `state.messages[session_id]` and returns the first `limit` items (line 157: `ordered.iter().take(limit)`). `query.cursor` is parsed by serde but ignored.
new_deviations_found.impact: Critical pagination bug: clients sending `?cursor=N` (where N was returned as cursor.next on a previous page) get the SAME first page again, not page N+1. This creates an infinite loop for clients that try to paginate. The opaque cursor encoding `limit.to_string()` is fine on the wire side, but the server never decodes/applies it. Severity: high — breaks a core contract feature.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:122, 138-176 — `query.cursor` is in the `SessionMessagesQuery` struct (line 94) but the handler only reads `query.order` (line 147) and `query.limit` (line 152). Lines 155-159 always take the first `limit` items, ignoring cursor.

new_deviations_found.contract_says: Each SessionMessage.Message variant (AgentSwitched, ModelSwitched, User, Synthetic, System, Shell, Assistant, Compaction) has its documented fields. output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are partially accurate but contain a significant framing error and miss a critical pagination bug. DEV-1 (response items are `{info, parts}` not flat `SessionMessage.Message`) is CONFIRMED — items lack the contract's `type` discriminator and use a Loom-specific projection. Severity `high` is correct. DEV-2 (404 body uses `_tag` vs `name`) is **PARTIALLY REJECTED on framing, CONFIRMED on missing error classes**. Re-read `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts:55-62`: `class SessionNotFoundError extends Schema.TaggedErrorClass<...>(\"SessionNotFoundError\", ...)` — Effect's `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` adds a `_tag` discriminator (with underscore prefix), NOT `name`. Loom's `_tag: \"SessionNotFoundError\"` IS the correct wire form. The auditor's claim \"uses `name`, not `_tag`\" is incorrect. The legitimate parts of DEV-2 are: `InvalidCursorError` and `UnknownError` never returned. DEV-3 (`cursor.previous` always null, default limit 50, cursor encoding is offset) is CONFIRMED for the first two sub-points. The third sub-point (cursor encoding is offset) is ALLOWED by the contract (cursors are opaque). DEV-4 (no brand validation) is CONFIRMED. **CRITICAL NEW FINDING: `query.cursor` is parsed but never read — pagination is broken**. The handler at `messages.rs:119-177` extracts `Query(query): Query<SessionMessagesQuery>` but `query.cursor` is never referenced in the handler body. Clients sending `?cursor=N` get the SAME first page, creating an infinite loop. The opaque cursor encoding `limit.to_string()` is fine on the wire side, but the server never decodes/applies it. Severity: high. The `partial` conformance classification is correct.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:100-114` (`project_message`) and `:155-159` (where it's invoked). Each item is constructed as `{info: <MessageInfo JSON>, parts: <Vec<Value>>}` — NOT the contract's flat `SessionMessage.Message` shape. The contract requires `data: SessionMessage.Message[]` where each item is a tagged union with `type` discriminator (one of 8 variants: agent-switched, model-switched, user, synthetic, system, shell, assistant, compaction — `packages/schema/src/session-message.ts:200-211`). Loom's items have NO `type` field on either `info` or `parts`. The `info` field is `serde_json::to_value(MessageInfo)` where `MessageInfo` (state.rs:320-363) is a flat record with `id`, `sessionID`, `role`, `time`, `agent`, `model`, `parentID`, `tool`, `finish`, `providerID`, `modelID`, etc. — none of which are the contract's `Base` (`id`, `time: {created}`, `metadata?`) or any of the 8 union members. Severity `high` is correct: v2 SDK clients will fail schema validation on every item.

PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — auditor framing is wrong, but legitimate parts stand. Re-read `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts:55-62`: `class SessionNotFoundError extends Schema.TaggedErrorClass<SessionNotFoundError>()(\"SessionNotFoundError\", { sessionID: Schema.String, message: Schema.String }, { httpApiStatus: 404 })`. ALL error classes in `errors.ts` use `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` — this is Effect's standard pattern that adds a `_tag` discriminator (with underscore prefix), NOT `name`. The auditor's claim \"uses `name`, not `_tag`\" is INCORRECT. Loom's `{\"_tag\": \"SessionNotFoundError\", \"sessionID\": ..., \"message\": ...}` matches the expected Effect wire form. The LEGITIMATE parts of DEV-2: (a) `InvalidCursorError` is declared for cursor+order combination (message.ts:36, errors.ts:74-78) and never returned by Loom; (b) `UnknownError` (500) is declared (errors.ts:37-44) and never returned. Severity for the legitimate parts: medium each. The auditor's framing \"404 body uses _tag instead of name\" should be REJECTED.

PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. (a) `cursor.previous` always `null` — CONFIRMED at `messages.rs:172` (`\"previous\": Value::Null`). Severity medium correct. (b) Default limit 50 — CONFIRMED at `messages.rs:152` (`query.limit.unwrap_or(50)`). Severity medium correct. (c) Cursor encoding is offset-as-string — CORRECT BUT MISLEADING. The contract marks cursors as opaque (`cursor: Schema.String.annotate({ description: \"Opaque pagination cursor...\" })`), so the format IS allowed. However, see NEW-1 — the cursor is NEVER HONORED by the server, which makes the encoding moot. Severity for the format itself: not a deviation (contract allows opaque). Severity for \"cursor not honored\": high (NEW-1).

CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:121`: `Path(session_id): Path<String>`. Cross-checked `packages/schema/src/session-id.ts`: `SessionID = Schema.String.check(Schema.isStartsWith(\"ses\")).pipe(...)`. The schema HAS `isStartsWith(\"ses\")` constraint. deviations.contract_says: Contract requires POST /api/session/:sessionID/permission/:requestID/reply to accept { reply, message? } and return 204 NoContent on success, 404 SessionNotFoundError or PermissionNotFoundError on failure.
deviations.loom_does: Route is not registered. Only TODO(W2) comment at routes.rs:925. Handler reply_session_permission (permission.rs:379) is fully implemented but unreachable.
deviations.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/routes.rs:925 (TODO comment); grep for '.route("/api/session/:sessionID/permission/:requestID/reply"' returns only TODO comment, no .route() call.
deviations.impact: CRITICAL: clients calling this endpoint receive 404 Not Found.

deviations.title: LS-011 BLOCKER: tool execution does not observe this reply
deviations.contract_says: Reply resolves a pending permission request. The resolved decision (allow/deny) is expected to be observable to tool execution: a denial should abort the tool, an allowance should permit it.
deviations.loom_does: Even if wired, tool execution does not consult the permission store to observe the reply. The LS-011 BLOCKER at permission.rs:19-27 applies to all session.permission.* endpoints. The handler emits permission.v2.replied SSE event for observers, but no observer (the Loom run path) currently subscribes.
deviations.impact: HIGH: even after W2, the permission system is structurally non-functional for its intended purpose. A user clicking "reject" on a permission request will not prevent the tool from executing.

deviations.title: "always" reply does not persist saved rule (no saved-rule write-through)
deviations.contract_says: reply="always" should persist a PermissionSaved.Info entry on the project for future auto-approval of the same action+resource.
deviations.loom_does: Handler transitions the internal PermissionRequest status to "approved"/"denied" but does NOT write a PermissionSaved.Info entry when reply="always". Per the handler code (after the session check), only the status is updated.
deviations.evidence_contract: packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts (reply "always" semantics are implicit in Permission.Reply type and the linked session.permission.create doc which mentions Saved permission rules)
deviations.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/permission.rs (read the reply handler body — status updated but no saved-rule insertion)
deviations.impact: MEDIUM: clients expecting "always" to remember the decision will see the next matching tool request still be "ask"-ed. The SavedPermissions store is not updated, so the saved ruleset stays empty. Operationally the "always" reply behaves identically to "once" — both are one-shot approvals that future requests still ask.

deviations.title: Loose payload validation — handler accepts malformed reply field
deviations.contract_says: Payload: { reply: Schema.Literals(["once", "always", "reject"]), message: Schema.optional(Schema.String) }. Schema rejects unknown reply values.
deviations.loom_does: Handler accepts Json<Value> with no schema validation. Any reply value is coerced: "once"|"always" → "approved", anything else (including malformed strings) → "denied". Handler does NOT return 400 for unknown values.
deviations.impact: LOW: clients sending reply="maybe" or reply=null get coerced to "denied" instead of 400. This is defensive (never accept unknown) but contract-conformant clients would expect 400 for unknown values. Severity is low because the contract doesn't have explicit error classes for "InvalidReplyError" — the handler's defensive coercion avoids a 500 at the cost of a silent denial.

missing_features: LS-011 tool execution permission hook (bridges this store to Loom's run path)
Saved-rule write-through when reply="always"
All 4 session.permission.* endpoints (create, list, get, reply) are W2 TODO — not just this one
extra_features: Cross-session security check: handler validates req.session_id == session_id and returns 404 PermissionNotFoundError (not SessionNotFoundError) on mismatch. This prevents leaking whether a request exists in another session. (matches defensive best practice)
message field accepted but not stored — used for logging/audit only
output.notes: Conformance level: NOT_IMPLEMENTED. Four deviations: 1 critical (route), 1 high (LS-011 BLOCKER), 1 medium (no saved-rule persistence), 1 low (loose payload validation). The handler is well-implemented: (a) cross-session 404 to prevent info leak, (b) defensive reply coercion (any unknown value → denied), (c) SSE event emission, (d) state transition. When W2 wires the route, two follow-up issues must be addressed: (1) LS-011 tool execution hook so replies are observed, (2) saved-rule write-through for reply="always". Without these, the permission system is structurally complete but operationally non-functional. The cross-session 404 mitigation is a good security practice that goes slightly beyond the contract.

output.overall_assessment: Re-verification from the boundary/edge-case angle. Boundary aspects: (a) Path traversal protection via lexical `normalize` + `starts_with(root)` check is correctly implemented; (b) Symlink following is NOT prevented — symlinks inside the root that point outside will be followed by `std::fs::read`, bypassing the lexical check (security boundary concern); (c) No file size limit — `std::fs::read` loads entire file into memory, so a multi-GB file would OOM; (d) IO error strings (e.g., "No such file or directory (os error 2)") are exposed verbatim in error bodies — minor info leak; (e) Whitespace-only path (`"  "`) is trimmed to empty, resolves to root, fails with 400 directory — defensible; (f) Missing path (no trailing wildcard) returns 404 from the router, not from the handler — correct routing behavior; (g) Concurrent reads serialize briefly on `state.project.read()` in `location_root` with no deadlock; (h) The handler is real (not v2_compat, not a placeholder); (i) No stale TODO(W2) comments in routes.rs for /api/fs/read.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: Verified. fs.rs:83, 137, 141, 152 all return `json!({"error": "..."})` body. Confirmed deviation from a TaggedErrorClass convention. However, the contract fs.ts:22-25 does NOT declare an `error: [...]` field for fs.read, so any shape is technically permitted by the contract. The deviation is more accurately classified as "internal-convention inconsistency": Loom's `session_not_found` (session.rs:30-40) uses `{ _tag, sessionID, message }` while fs handlers use `{ error: msg }`. For a strict boundary review, this matters because clients cannot pattern-match on `_tag` for fs errors — they must use HTTP status codes. Severity "medium" is reasonable.

Verified. routes.rs:261 uses `/api/fs/read/*path` (named wildcard), contract fs.ts:22 uses `/api/fs/read/*` (anonymous wildcard). Both capture trailing path segments identically in axum 0.7+ — the name is binding the segment to a variable, which `read` then extracts via `Path(path): Path<String>` (fs.rs:122). Cosmetic-only. Severity "low" is correct.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: C:/Users/heycj/dev/opencode/packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:31 — `description: "Serve one file relative to the requested location."` — semantically implies the file must be under the location directory.
new_deviations_found.impact: If a user has a symlink in their location root pointing outside (e.g., `/work/secrets -> /etc/secrets`), they can read the target via `/api/fs/read/secrets/passwd`. Lexical `normalize` does not detect this — only `std::fs::canonicalize` would. Loom's path-traversal protection is incomplete for symlink cases. Whether this is a contract violation depends on whether symlink-aware safety is required — the contract says "relative to the requested location" which is semantically violated by an external symlink.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Files must be "relative to the requested location" — semantically under the location directory.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `resolve_within` (fs.rs:66-86) uses `normalize` which is purely lexical (`Component::CurDir`/`ParentDir` handling, no filesystem access). It does NOT call `canonicalize` on the requested path. So a symlink inside the root that lexically appears inside but points outside passes the check, and `std::fs::read` follows the symlink.
new_deviations_found.title: Symlink following allows escape beyond the lexical path-traversal check
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:66-86 (`resolve_within` uses `normalize` only, no canonicalize); fs.rs:147 `std::fs::read(&resolved)` follows symlinks.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: C:/Users/heycj/dev/opencode/packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:24 — `success: Schema.Uint8Array.pipe(HttpApiSchema.asUint8Array())` — Uint8Array implies binary data, but no size constraint declared.
new_deviations_found.impact: A malicious client could request `/api/fs/read/large-database.bin` and trigger OOM if the file is multi-GB. The handler reads the entire file into memory via `std::fs::read` with no streaming and no size cap. For a dev tool this is acceptable; for production this is a DoS vector.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `success: Schema.Uint8Array` — no size constraint, no streaming requirement.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: fs.rs:147 `std::fs::read(&resolved)` loads the entire file into a `Vec<u8>`. No `take()` limit, no streaming, no async chunked read. Memory usage = file size.
new_deviations_found.title: No file size limit; entire file loaded into memory

new_deviations_found.impact: Server returns raw `std::io::Error::to_string()` in error bodies. On Linux for ENOENT: `"No such file or directory (os error 2)"`. Exposing OS error strings reveals implementation details (filesystem type, OS version via error message format). Minor info leak.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No error classes declared; no specific error body shape required.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: fs.rs:137, 152, 240, 253, 284, 300, 334, 345, 375 — all use `Json(json!({"error": e.to_string()}))` where `e` is a `std::io::Error`. The full OS error string is exposed verbatim.

new_deviations_found.impact: Unauthenticated clients can read any file under the location directory (and via symlinks, any file the server process has access to). For dev/integration this is acceptable; for production this is a security concern. The contract is silent on auth for fs.read (no auth requirement declared), so this is forward-looking only.

new_deviations_found.impact: Empty/whitespace location strings reach the handler and resolve to the server's default project directory. No rejection, no error. Clients sending malformed location queries get the same response as clients sending valid ones.

new_deviations_found.title: `LocationQuery` accepts empty/whitespace values; falls back to server default
`after` accepts u64 but contract requires `NonNegativeInt` (capped at i32::MAX)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `after: Schema.NumberFromString.pipe(Schema.decodeTo(NonNegativeInt), Schema.optional)` (`session.ts:330`). `NonNegativeInt = Schema.Int.check(Schema.isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(0))` is capped at i32::MAX (~2.1 billion).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `api_session_event_stream` at `sse.rs:65`: `let after = match query.after.as_deref().unwrap_or(\"0\").parse::<u64>() { ... }`. Accepts any u64 value up to 2^64-1.
new_deviations_found.impact: Boundary gap: clients sending values > i32::MAX (~2.1 billion) would be accepted by Loom but fail contract validation. For practical cursor advancement, this is extremely rare. Severity `low`.

new_deviations_found.title: `location` field is `Option<Value>`, not typed `Location.Ref`
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `location?: Location.Ref` where `Location.Ref = { directory: AbsolutePath, workspaceID?: WorkspaceID, project: { id: ProjectID, directory: AbsolutePath } }` (`schema/event.ts:38`, `schema/location.ts:14-21`).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `V2Event.location: Option<Value>` (`v2_event.rs:39-40`) — untyped JSON value. Currently Loom always sets `location: None` (line 193), so the field is always omitted via `skip_serializing_if = \"Option::is_none\"`.
new_deviations_found.impact: Data gap: if a publisher sets `location` to a malformed JSON value, the contract's `Location.Ref` schema would reject it. Currently no publisher sets location, so no impact in practice. Severity `low` (defensive).

new_deviations_found.title: V2_LOG_CAP = 2,048 events per session; older events evicted
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No explicit retention contract text.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `v2_event.rs:19` (`const V2_LOG_CAP: usize = 2_048`) and `:211-213` (`if log.len() == V2_LOG_CAP { log.pop_front(); }`). Replay limited to the most recent 2,048 events.
new_deviations_found.impact: Operational constraint: replay beyond 2,048 events impossible. Clients with `after` < (current_seq - 2048) get nothing. Severity `informational` (architecture, not a contract violation).

new_deviations_found.title: `seq` counter uses u64 with wrapping add; `v2_next_seq` increments without bound
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Contract's `durable.seq: Schema.Int` is i32.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `v2_event.rs:139` (`*next = next.wrapping_add(1)`); `:216` (`state.v2_next_seq.write().insert(session_id, seq + 1)`). On overflow, sequence wraps.
new_deviations_found.impact: Boundary gap: after 2^64 events, sequences wrap to 0. Clients expecting monotonically increasing sequence numbers would see sudden reset. Severity `low` (extremely rare in practice).

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/sse.rs:60-78, 135-162, 164-169`, `apps/server/src/v2_event.rs:30-42`, `apps/server/src/routes.rs:481-482`, and `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:327-345` confirms all 5 deviations: (1) DEV-1 (SessionNotFoundError never returned) is HIGH severity correctly identified — handler at sse.rs:60-78 has no session existence check; (2) DEV-2 (sessionLocationMiddleware not applied) is MEDIUM correctly identified — routes.rs:481-482 has no .layer; (3) DEV-3 (no `ses_` brand validation) is LOW correctly identified — Path<String> at sse.rs:62; (4) DEV-4 (400 plain text on invalid `after`) is LOW correctly identified — sse.rs:67-73; (5) DEV-5 (stale TODO at routes.rs:909) is LOW correctly identified. Schema analysis: V2Event struct (v2_event.rs:30-42) serializes to `{id, type (renamed from event_type), data, durable?, location?, metadata?}` which matches the contract's Event.Payload shape EXACTLY. Event IDs are `evt_v2_*` starting with `evt_` matching the Event.ID brand (`schema/event.ts:9-12`). V2Durable uses `aggregateID` rename matching contract's `durable.aggregateID`. SSE framing uses standard `Event::default().event("message").data(data)`. Found 4 new findings: (1) `after` accepts u64 but contract requires NonNegativeInt (i32::MAX cap), boundary gap (low); (2) `location` field is `Option<Value>` not typed `Location.Ref` (low, defensive); (3) V2_LOG_CAP = 2,048 events per session, replay limit (informational); (4) `seq` uses u64 with wrapping add, sequence wrap-around risk (low). The auditor's `partial` conformance classification is correct.

new_deviations_found.title: Group-level `locationMiddleware` not applied to `/api/permission/saved` route
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `HttpApiGroup.make(\"server.permission\")...add(permission.saved.list).add(permission.saved.remove).middleware(locationMiddleware).add(session.permission.*)` (`permission.ts:21-87`). The comment at line 60 states: \"Effect applies group middleware only to endpoints already added\". The `.middleware(locationMiddleware)` chain is positioned AFTER the first three `.add()` calls (request.list, saved.list, saved.remove) and BEFORE the session endpoints — so `locationMiddleware` is expected to apply to `permission.saved.list`.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `/api/permission/saved` is registered as `.route(\"/api/permission/saved\", get(handlers::health::get_permission_saved))` (`routes.rs:317-321`) with no `.layer(...)` for any middleware. The handler signature `pub async fn get_permission_saved() -> Json<Value>` (`health.rs:25-27`) takes NO extractors at all — no `State`, no `Query`, nothing.
new_deviations_found.impact: Schema deviation in middleware handling: the contract expects `locationMiddleware` to be applied. Loom doesn't apply any. However, since the handler doesn't read state or query, the missing middleware has no observable effect on the response (the response is hardcoded `{data: []}`). Severity `low` because no client can detect the missing middleware from the wire response. The deviation would matter if/when the handler is replaced with a real implementation that reads state.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/routes.rs:317-321 (no middleware layer); apps/server/src/handlers/health.rs:25-27 (handler takes no extractors).
new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: C:/Users/heycj/dev/opencode/packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts:60-61 — `.middleware(locationMiddleware)` applied between the saved.* and session.* endpoints.

new_deviations_found.title: Always-empty `data: []` is a placeholder; no real saved permission store
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `success: Schema.Struct({ data: Schema.Array(PermissionSaved.Info) })` (`permission.ts:39`). The contract expects a real list of `PermissionSaved.Info` records filtered by `projectID` if provided.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler always returns `{ \"data\": [] }` (`health.rs:25-27`). No state read, no store access. The endpoint is a hardcoded empty placeholder.
new_deviations_found.impact: Wire-shape conformant (empty array is valid per `Schema.Array`). Data-completeness gap: no real saved permissions are ever returned. Clients cannot enumerate saved permissions via this endpoint. The audit's `partial` classification is correct.

new_deviations_found.title: `PermissionSaved.Info.id` brand — `psv_` prefix only via static creator, not enforced
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `PermissionSaved.ID = Schema.String.pipe(Schema.brand(\"PermissionSaved.ID\"), statics((schema) => ({ create: () => schema.make(\"psv_\" + ascending()) })))` (`schema/permission-saved.ts:8-11`). The `create()` static returns `\"psv_\" + ascending()`, but the brand itself has no `isStartsWith(\"psv_\")` check.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: No validation. The handler doesn't generate IDs (returns empty array). If a real implementation were wired, it would need to use the `create()` static to generate conformant IDs.
new_deviations_found.impact: Wire-level: brand strips on encode, so any string is accepted. The `psv_` prefix is convention, not enforcement. Low severity because the handler is currently empty.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's DEV-1 is accurate and well-evidenced. Independent re-reading of `packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts:36-46` (contract), `apps/server/src/handlers/health.rs:25-27` (handler), and `apps/server/src/routes.rs:317-321` (route) confirms: (a) the contract declares `query: Schema.Struct({ projectID: Project.ID.pipe(Schema.optional) })`; (b) the handler takes NO parameters at all — no `Query<...>` extractor, no `State<...>`, no path params; (c) `projectID` is silently dropped; (d) the response is hardcoded `{data: []}`. Severity `medium` is correct. The `partial` conformance classification is correct — envelope shape is conformant (bare `{data: ...}` per contract, NOT `Location.response`), but data is always empty. Schema check: (1) bare envelope `{data: Schema.Array(...)}` correctly produced; (2) NO `Location.response` wrapping (correct — contract declares `Schema.Struct({data: ...})`, not `Location.response`); (3) no `locationQueryOpenApi` annotation (correct — contract doesn't declare it for this endpoint); (4) `PermissionSaved.Info` is NOT a tagged union (flat struct), no tag handling needed; (5) `PermissionSaved.Info.id` has brand `PermissionSaved.ID` with `psv_` prefix convention (via `create()` static) but no `isStartsWith` check (wire-level strips brand, so any string accepted). Found 3 low-severity new findings: (a) `locationMiddleware` not applied at route (group-level middleware expected per `permission.ts:60-61`), (b) always-empty data is a placeholder, (c) brand prefix not enforced.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED. Re-read `packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts:37-46`: the contract declares `query: Schema.Struct({ projectID: Project.ID.pipe(Schema.optional) })`. Cross-checked `apps/server/src/handlers/health.rs:25-27`: `pub async fn get_permission_saved() -> Json<Value> { Json(json!({ \"data\": [] })) }` — the handler takes NO parameters at all. The `projectID` query is silently dropped. The endpoint always returns `{data: []}`. Severity `medium` is correct: clients sending `?projectID=foo` expect filtered results but get empty array. The filtering feature is non-functional. The wire form (`{data: []}`) is conformant (empty array is valid per `Schema.Array`), but the data-completeness gap makes the endpoint non-functional. new_deviations_found.title: Concurrent prompts on same session run as separate agent-loops, never conflict
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: [ConflictError, SessionNotFoundError]` (`session.ts:214`). ConflictError should be 409 when the session is busy in a way that rejects input.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `prompt_v2` at `session.rs:218-457` does not check session busy state. Two concurrent POSTs to the same session both succeed (200), both call `tokio::spawn(run_agent)`, both create separate user messages, both register separate abort tokens via `begin_run`. The last `begin_run` overwrites the prior abort token (since `state.abort_tokens.read().get(&session_id)` returns the latest). Cancellation state is shared and corrupted.
new_deviations_found.impact: Boundary: under concurrent prompts, both run in parallel. The second `begin_run` overwrites the first's abort token, so cancelling one session cancels the other. This is the runtime manifestation of DEV-1. Severity `medium` because the issue is functionally observable.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:322 (unconditional tokio::spawn); :361 (unconditional begin_run, overwrites prior abort_tokens[session_id] entry).

new_deviations_found.title: Empty `prompt.text` produces no-op user message + runs agent-loop with empty input
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `PromptInput.Prompt.text: Schema.String` (required). A client sending `{prompt: {}}` should be rejected.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `session.rs:225-229`: `prompt_text` defaults to `\"\"` if missing. Handler still creates a user message with empty text, stores an empty text part, and spawns the agent-loop with empty input.
new_deviations_found.impact: Functional gap: a client sending `{prompt: {}}` (or with empty text) sees a 200 response with a \"successful\" admission. The user message has empty content; the agent receives an empty prompt. Downstream consumers see \"no-op user messages.\" This compounds with DEV-2 (text not validated as required). Severity `medium` because the issue is functionally observable.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:225-229 (`unwrap_or_default().to_string()`); :305-308 (empty text part stored); :322 (tokio::spawn with empty prompt).

new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on max length.

new_deviations_found.title: Body without `prompt` field silently falls through to v1 path

deviations.title: Placeholder returns 501 Not Implemented instead of contract's 200 OK with Location.response wrapped Pty.Info
deviations.contract_says: Contract requires PUT /api/pty/:ptyID with payload Pty.UpdateInput = { title?, size?: { rows: PositiveInt, cols: PositiveInt } }. On success returns 200 OK with body Schema.Struct({ data: Location.response(Pty.Info) }). On 404 returns PtyNotFoundError(404) with { ptyID, message }.
deviations.loom_does: Route is registered (routes.rs:279 put(handlers::mcp_pty_file::put_pty_one)), but the handler is a placeholder returning 501 Not Implemented with body { error: "PTY update not implemented" }. The full handler implementation exists at apps/server/src/handlers/pty.rs:359+ (per module docs) but is NOT wired. The route comment at routes.rs:269-270 explicitly says: "Contract-shaped /api/pty* routes. Handlers live in mcp_pty_file.rs as honest 501s until handlers/pty.rs ships the full lifecycle."
deviations.evidence_contract: packages/protocol/src/groups/pty.ts:64-78 (HttpApiEndpoint.put with ptyID param, payload, success, error)
deviations.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/routes.rs:269-289 (route registration as placeholder); apps/server/src/handlers/mcp_pty_file.rs:94-102 (placeholder handler returning 501)
deviations.impact: HIGH: clients conforming to the contract (expecting 200 with Location.response) will get 501 with handler-specific body. The endpoint is fundamentally non-functional despite being routed. While 501 is "honest" (it doesn't fake success), the body shape is not the contract's error class shape (PtyNotFoundError is also not returned for missing PTY — clients get 501 instead of 404). This is a stronger deviation than a 400/404 body shape issue — the entire response semantic is wrong.

missing_features: Real PTY update implementation (handlers/pty.rs:359+ has full update, but unwired)

Payload validation (Pty.UpdateInput: title?, size?: { rows: PositiveInt, cols: PositiveInt })

output.notes: Conformance level: NON_CONFORMANT. This is the first endpoint in my audit series classified as non_conformant (vs not_implemented for missing route/handler, or partial for handler-specific deviations). The route IS registered (routing works), but the handler returns 501 with a body shape that doesn't match the contract's error class. The full handler at apps/server/src/handlers/pty.rs:359+ is implemented but not wired — the route comment at routes.rs:269-270 explicitly states "Handlers live in mcp_pty_file.rs as honest 501s until handlers/pty.rs ships the full lifecycle." When the wiring happens (likely a single-line change in routes.rs), the endpoint would likely become largely conformant. The severity is "high" (not "critical") because the route is registered and the placeholder is honest about its incompleteness — clients can detect and handle 501 without crashing. Notable: this is the first endpoint where the 501 status is structurally important (the handler code accepts _id and _body but immediately returns 501 without doing anything — it's a true placeholder, not a partial implementation).

new_deviations_found.title: Cursor parsed but NEVER USED — pagination is broken
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `cursor?: string` in `SessionMessagesQuery` (`message.ts:16-21`). Cursor is opaque pagination token returned as `cursor.next` or `cursor.previous` in the previous response. The contract marks cursors as opaque but expects them to advance pagination: \"use cursor.next or cursor.previous to move through the ordered timeline.\"
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `SessionMessagesQuery.cursor: Option<String>` (`messages.rs:94`) is deserialized but NEVER consulted in the handler body (lines 119-177). The handler always starts from the beginning of the messages list (after optional reverse for desc). The `next_cursor` returned is `Some(limit.to_string())` (`messages.rs:163-167`) — just the limit value, NOT an actual offset.
new_deviations_found.impact: MAJOR BUG: pagination is non-functional. Client flow: (1) GET /api/session/X/message?limit=10 → returns 10 messages, cursor.next=\"10\". (2) GET /api/session/X/message?limit=10&cursor=10 → client expects messages 11-20, but cursor is ignored, so client gets the same first 10 messages again. Clients can never page past the first page. This is a major functional deviation, not just a wire-shape deviation. Severity high because the endpoint's primary use case (paging through conversation history) is broken.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:94 (cursor field deserialized), :138-159 (handler body — `cursor` not referenced anywhere in the data fetch logic), :163-167 (next_cursor is just `limit.to_string()`, not a real offset).

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are partially correct but contain a critical false-positive framing. DEV-1, DEV-3, DEV-4 are confirmed. new_deviations_found.title: Server-wide auth middleware applies to /api/health — monitoring probes get 401 if LOOM_AUTH_TOKEN is set
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Contract declares no middleware on `health.get`. The OpenAPI summary says "Check whether the API server is ready to accept requests" — implying the endpoint should be reachable for probes.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `apps/server/src/routes.rs:944` applies `.layer(middleware::from_fn(require_valid_token))` to the entire router (all routes, including `/api/health`). If `LOOM_AUTH_TOKEN` is configured, an unauthenticated `GET /api/health` returns 401 instead of 200.
new_deviations_found.impact: Operational concern: external monitoring systems probing server health will be rejected when the API is locked down with a token. The contract doesn't explicitly require health to be unauthenticated, so this is conformant per the contract text — but it diverges from the operational expectation that health probes are unauthenticated. Low severity because (a) the contract doesn't forbid this behavior and (b) the auth middleware is documented as conditional (dev mode bypass).

new_deviations_found.title: Health check is unconditional — no readiness check for DB / providers / state
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Description: \"Check whether the API server is ready to accept requests.\" The closed literal schema `Schema.Literal(true)` means only `{healthy: true}` is a valid success response.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `apps/server/src/handlers/health.rs:12-19` is a constant `Json(json!({\"healthy\": true}))`. There is no DB connection check, no provider list validation, no state-store verification, no async initialization check. The response is computed at request time but always returns the same value regardless of server state.
new_deviations_found.impact: Shallow readiness check. A degraded server (DB down, providers not loaded, persistent store failing to open) will still return `{healthy: true}`. For a kernel liveness probe this is fine (the HTTP layer is up); for a deep readiness probe it's insufficient. The contract's closed literal schema forces Loom to return `true` even when degraded — there's no way for the implementation to signal \"I'm up but not ready\" because the contract only allows `true`. Low severity: informational only; the contract itself limits the response to `healthy: true`.

output.overall_assessment: Re-verification from the boundary/edge-case angle. The critical finding from my previous review holds: **DEV-1 is a FALSE POSITIVE**. The auditor cited "credential.rs:104-113" as evidence for `remove_credential` returning 404, but those lines (104-113) of the actual file are the body of `remove_credential` which UNCONDITIONALLY returns `StatusCode::NO_CONTENT` (line 112). The 404 with `{ error, credentialID }` body lives in `update_credential` at lines 81-89, NOT in `remove_credential`. The two handlers have INCONSISTENT unknown-id behavior — PATCH returns 404, DELETE returns 204 — but neither violates the contract (no `error: [...]` declared on either endpoint). From the boundary angle: (a) Garbage credentialIDs (whitespace, non-`cred_` prefixed, very long, unicode) are silently accepted as no-op lookups returning 204; this is consistent with opencode's wire-transparent brand treatment. (b) The write lock is acquired only for the duration of `HashMap::remove` (single syscall); no deadlock or starvation risk. (c) Concurrent DELETEs serialize on the lock with no race. (d) No stale TODO(W2) comments in routes.rs for credential paths. (e) Handler is not v2_compat / not a placeholder — real implementation reading from `state.credentials`.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: REJECTED again — same false positive as in the previous review. Lines 104-113 of the actual `remove_credential` handler: signature at 104-108, write-lock + HashMap.remove at 109, TODO comment at 110-111, unconditional `StatusCode::NO_CONTENT` return at 112. There is NO 404 branch in `remove_credential`. The 404 path the auditor cites belongs to `update_credential` at lines 81-89. From a boundary angle specifically: `remove_credential` for an unknown id ALWAYS returns 204 (verified by reading the code) — there is no 404 body to be conformant or non-conformant about. The auditor's evidence-claim that "remove_credential: returns StatusCode::NOT_FOUND with json!({ error, credentialID })" is factually wrong about this endpoint.

For boundary angle: this is an OPERATIONAL boundary — restart loses state. From a pure edge-case angle, every successful DELETE is permanent within the process lifetime but not across restart. Severity "medium" is appropriate.

output.notes: Route `/api/session/:sessionID/context` (GET) is registered at `apps/server/src/routes.rs:436-438` and wired to `handlers::session::get_context` (`session.rs:686-722`) — a real handler reading from `state.messages` and `state.parts`. The handler returns 200 with `Json({"data": [...]})` where each item is `{info: MessageInfo, parts: [Value]}` rather than the contract's flat `SessionMessage.Message` objects with a `type` discriminator. `SessionNotFoundError` (404) is correctly produced via `session_not_found()` (`session.rs:30-40`). `UnknownError` (500) is never returned (no try/except wraps the projection; serde failures return `Value::Null` silently). `LocationQuery` is parsed via `_loc: Query<LocationQuery>` (functionally mirrors the contract's `sessionLocationMiddleware`). No auth middleware → `UnauthorizedError` is never returned. No compaction logic; all messages are returned regardless of "active context" semantics.

side_effects.notes: Read-only GET. No SSE events emitted. State is not mutated. Multiple GETs are idempotent — `state.messages.read()` returns the same snapshot each time (modulo concurrent writes from `prompt`/`patch`). No atomicity concerns (no mutations).

route_registration.notes: Registered at `apps/server/src/routes.rs:436-438` as `.route("/api/session/:sessionID/context", get(handlers::session::get_context))`. Path matches contract (`HttpApiEndpoint.get("session.context", "/api/session/:sessionID/context", ...)` at session.ts:292). Method matches (GET). Handler is real (`get_context` is fully implemented, not v2_compat, not TODO). There is a stale TODO comment at `routes.rs:913` referencing this route, but the actual registration at line 436 is live.

query_params.notes: Path param `:sessionID` is extracted correctly via `Path<String>` (`session.rs:691`). Contract specifies `params: { sessionID: Session.ID }` (branded `ses_`-prefixed string). Loom extracts it as a plain `String` — no `isStartsWith("ses")` brand check is performed. `_loc: Query<LocationQuery>` correctly accepts the optional location query parameter that the contract's `sessionLocationMiddleware` is meant to parse (functionally conforms, though not named middleware). No cursor pagination is declared in the contract for this endpoint, so no deviation.

payload_validation.notes: No request body (GET). No validation of `sessionID` brand. An invalid sessionID (no `ses_` prefix, or unknown id) is accepted but produces 404 from the store lookup — which is acceptable behavior, though the contract's branded type would reject the request earlier.

error_handling.notes: `SessionNotFoundError` IS returned with status 404 and body `{_tag: "SessionNotFoundError", sessionID, message}` (`session.rs:30-40, 694-696`). Matches contract's expected error shape (Effect discriminated error with `_tag` field). `UnknownError` (500) is declared by the contract (`session.ts:295`) but never produced — `serde_json::to_value` failures are swallowed with `.unwrap_or(Value::Null)` rather than converted to a 500 (`session.rs:715`). `UnauthorizedError` (401, server-wide) is never produced (no auth middleware wired).

status_code.notes: 200 OK on success (axum Json default). 404 on missing session via `session_not_found()` returning `StatusCode::NOT_FOUND`. No 500 path. NoContent (204) is not applicable (response has body).

middleware.notes: Contract chains `.middleware(sessionLocationMiddleware)` (`session.ts:297`). Loom does not have a named middleware but functionally mirrors it by accepting `_loc: Query<LocationQuery>` (`session.rs:692`) — this parses the same location query parameters that the middleware would inject, then ignores the value (response is bare). Functionally conforms; architecturally deviates from the contract's middleware annotation. No auth middleware is applied (contract has none here either, since `UnauthorizedError` is server-wide).

response_shape.notes: CRITICAL: Loom returns `{ data: Array<{info: MessageInfo, parts: Value[]}> }` while the contract requires `{ data: SessionMessage.Message[] }` where each `Message` is a tagged union by `type` (one of 8 variants: agent-switched, model-switched, user, synthetic, system, shell, assistant, compaction — session.ts:48-59). Loom's items have NO `type` field on either `info` or `parts`. The `info` field is `serde_json::to_value(MessageInfo)` where `MessageInfo` (state.rs:320-363) is a flat record with `id`, `sessionID`, `role`, `time`, `agent`, `model`, `parentID`, `tool`, `finish`, `providerID`, `modelID`, `cost`, `tokens`, etc. — none of which are the contract's `Base` (`id`, `time: {created}`, `metadata?`) or any of the 8 union members. Loom's `time` is `serde_json::Value` (state.rs:326), not the typed `DateTimeUtcFromMillis` struct required by `Base`. The `parts` field is opaque JSON per item — the contract's `Message` does not have a top-level `parts` array (parts live inside `assistant.content[].tool.state.content[]`). At least 4 of the 8 contract message variants (`agent-switched`, `model-switched`, `synthetic`, `shell`, `compaction`) cannot be represented in Loom's `MessageInfo` shape at all.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor correctly identified that `credential.update` is a real (not placeholder) handler with a genuine in-memory implementation. The conformance is `partial`, primarily because of the durability gap. Verifying the two reported deviations: DEV-1 (404 body shape) is REJECTED — the contract does NOT declare any error class for `credential.update` (credential.ts:8-22 has no `error: [...]` field), so the handler's `{ error, credentialID }` body is conformant by silence — there is no spec to violate. DEV-2 (no persistence) is CONFIRMED with severity upgraded from medium to HIGH — the contract's `summary: "Update a stored credential label"` and `description: "Update a stored credential label."` both use the word "stored", which semantically implies durability; clients cannot rely on the mutation surviving restart, which is a material behavior gap in production. From a behavior angle, I found five additional issues the auditor missed — most importantly that the handler emits NO SSE event on mutation (silent state change while sibling handlers like `session.create` do emit), and that the brand prefix `cred_` is never validated (a client bug surfaces as 404 instead of 400). The handler IS concurrency-safe (parking_lot RwLock serializes writes), is NOT auth-bypassed (router-level `require_valid_token` applies), and is NOT state-leaky (scoped to the credential store only).

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: REJECTED. Re-read credential.ts:8-22 — the endpoint definition is `{ params: { credentialID: Credential.ID }, query: LocationQuery, payload: Schema.Struct({ label: Schema.String }), success: HttpApiSchema.NoContent }`. There is NO `error: [...]` field on this endpoint. The contract is entirely silent on error responses. The handler returns a sensible 404 with `{ error: "credential not found", credentialID }` (credential.rs:81-89) — since the contract doesn't specify an error shape, the handler cannot violate one. The auditor's own evidence quote admits this: "(no error: field on endpoint)". A deviation requires a contract clause to deviate FROM; an unspecified case is not a violation. The handler's choice to return JSON with `error` + `credentialID` is reasonable REST practice and consistent with how other Loom handlers emit 404 (e.g. session_not_found at session.rs:30-40 uses `{ _tag: "SessionNotFoundError", sessionID, message }` — same pattern). Not a deviation.

CONFIRMED, severity upgraded from medium to HIGH. Re-read the handler module docs (credential.rs:21-41) and handler body (credential.rs:73-95): the in-memory store is the only backing, no `persist_credential` helper exists, no Store trait method for credentials is wired. The auditor's claim is verified. The contract's `summary` and `description` both say "stored credential" — the word "stored" implies durability. A client that updates a credential, restarts the server, and finds it gone will treat this as data loss. In production this is a critical operational gap (OAuth refresh tokens, API keys disappear on restart). The handler's own module docs acknowledge this as a known gap ("we do not fake a write-through") — that's an honest disclosure, but it doesn't change the fact that behavior diverges from the implicit contract semantics. Severity HIGH is appropriate because: (a) the impact is data loss in production; (b) the failure mode is silent (204 success but data gone); (c) recovery requires recreating credentials manually. The auditor's "medium" classification undersells the production impact.

CONFIRMED with corrected severity. Handler signature at credential.rs:106 is `Path(credential_id): Path<String>` — confirmed. However, the auditor's framing is misleading: the contract's `Credential.ID` schema (credential.ts:9-12) is `Schema.String.pipe(Schema.brand("Credential.ID"), statics(...))` with NO `Schema.isStartsWith("cred_")` check. The `cred_` prefix is only enforced by the `create()` static factory. So on the wire, the contract itself is permissive — any string is acceptable as `Credential.ID`. The lack of `cred_` validation in Loom matches the contract's actual (non-)enforcement. Severity should be "informational" rather than "low" — both sides are equally permissive.

new_deviations_found.title: 5-minute timeout result silently discarded; no way to distinguish idle-completion from timeout
new_deviations_found.contract_says: error: [SessionNotFoundError, ServiceUnavailableError] (session.ts:244). ServiceUnavailableError (503) should be returned when the agent loop fails to become idle (timeout, crash, etc.).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: session.rs:672-682: let _ = tokio::time::timeout(timeout, async { ... }).await; — the timeout Result is bound to _ (discarded). On timeout, the handler continues to StatusCode::NO_CONTENT.into_response() as if the agent loop had completed normally. The polling loop also has no way to detect an agent-loop crash — lookup_run returns Some when a run exists, regardless of whether the run is healthy or has crashed.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: clients cannot tell normal completion from 5-minute timeout. Severity medium (functional gap; this refines DEV-2). Same root cause as DEV-2 but more specific about the mechanism.

new_deviations_found.title: No way to cancel a wait; only signal is 5-minute timeout
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on cancellation.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler holds the HTTP connection open for up to 5 minutes. The client can only terminate the wait by dropping the HTTP connection (which would cause axum to cancel the handler task) or by waiting for the timeout.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: clients that want to abort a wait (e.g., on user navigation) can only do so by closing the connection. axum will cancel the handler task, but the Tokio runtime may still process the in-flight tokio::time::sleep before cancellation propagates. Severity low (no functional break).

new_deviations_found.title: No limit on concurrent waiters per session; each polls independently
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on waiter limits.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Multiple concurrent POSTs to /wait for the same sessionID would each independently poll lookup_run at 100ms intervals. The state.runs lookup is a parking_lot read lock, so concurrent reads are safe but the load scales linearly with waiter count.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: a client could spawn many concurrent wait requests, each adding load to the state.runs lookup. Severity low (no correctness break, performance concern). If 1000 clients wait for the same session, the state.runs lookup runs 10000 times per second.

new_deviations_found.title: Fixed 100ms polling cadence with no exponential backoff
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on polling cadence.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: tokio::time::sleep(100ms) per iteration (session.rs:678). Constant cadence regardless of expected wait duration.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: long waits use more CPU than necessary. Exponential backoff (e.g., 100ms, 200ms, 400ms, ...) would reduce load. Severity informational (no functional break).
