output.summary: Connect PTY (WebSocket); route registered but returns 426 instead of upgrading; auth bypass + ticket validation missing.

item.notes: Route is registered with GET method, but the handler is a placeholder returning 426. WebSocket upgrade is not implemented.

deviations.title: Placeholder returns 426 Upgrade Required; contract requires 200 OK with Schema.Boolean success
deviations.contract_says: Contract requires GET /api/pty/:ptyID/connect to upgrade the HTTP connection to WebSocket (101 Switching Protocols per RFC 6455). On success: 200 with body Schema.Boolean (or 101 + WS frames). On error: 403 ForbiddenError or 404 PtyNotFoundError. The OpenAPI transform annotates the endpoint as "x-websocket": true with custom query parameters.
deviations.loom_does: Route is registered (routes.rs:287 get(handlers::mcp_pty_file::get_api_pty_connect)), but the handler is a placeholder returning 426 Upgrade Required with body { error: "PTY WebSocket connect requires upgrade; not yet implemented" }. No actual WebSocket upgrade is performed. The body is neither Schema.Boolean nor the contract's error class shapes.
deviations.evidence_contract: packages/protocol/src/groups/pty.ts:119-141 (HttpApiEndpoint.get with success: Schema.Boolean, error: [ForbiddenError, PtyNotFoundError], x-websocket: true annotation, custom query params)
deviations.impact: HIGH: clients conforming to the contract will expect either (a) a successful WebSocket connection (101 + WS frames), or (b) a ForbiddenError(403) / PtyNotFoundError(404) on failure. They will instead receive 426 with a handler-specific body. The 426 status is technically correct for "client should upgrade", but it does not actually upgrade — clients following the contract will hang on the response without getting the WebSocket stream. This is a structural non-conformance.

deviations.title: Ticket-based auth bypass not implemented; Authorization middleware will reject all requests
deviations.contract_says: Contract has a special auth bypass: Authorization middleware skips credential checks when URL matches /^\/api\/pty\/[^/]+\/connect$/ AND ?ticket=... is present. The PTY connect handler is then responsible for ticket validation. Custom header x-opencode-ticket: 1 is also required for ticket issuance (PTY_CONNECT_TOKEN_HEADER = "x-opencode-ticket").
deviations.loom_does: Loom's mcp_pty_file handler accepts the path param but does NOT check for ticket presence. The ticket-based auth bypass logic from opencode's middleware (hasPtyConnectTicketURL) is NOT implemented in Loom. Clients sending ?ticket=... would still be rejected by Loom's standard Authorization middleware.
deviations.evidence_contract: packages/protocol/src/groups/pty.ts:9-19 (PTY_CONNECT_TICKET_QUERY, PTY_CONNECT_TOKEN_HEADER, hasPtyConnectTicketURL function); errors.ts (ForbiddenError definition)
deviations.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/mcp_pty_file.rs:126-131 (handler body accepts _id only, no ticket check)
deviations.impact: HIGH: the contract's auth bypass is structural to the PTY WebSocket flow. Without it, no client can connect. The flow is: (1) client calls pty.connectToken to get a ticket, (2) client opens WebSocket to pty.connect?ticket=..., (3) Authorization middleware sees the ticket and skips credential check, (4) PTY connect handler validates ticket and establishes stream. Loom has step 1 (placeholder) and step 4 (placeholder), but no step 3 — even with the ticket, the standard auth middleware would reject the request.

deviations.title: PtyNotFoundError(404) and ForbiddenError(403) not returned; only 426 path exists
deviations.contract_says: Contract declares two error classes: ForbiddenError(403) with { message, kind } and PtyNotFoundError(404) with { ptyID, message }. These should be returned for ticket validation failures and unknown ptyID respectively.
deviations.loom_does: Handler always returns 426 regardless of the request state. Even if the path param is an unknown ptyID, the client receives 426 (not 404). Even if the ticket is invalid, the client receives 426 (not 403). The body shape is { error: "..." } — not the contract's error class shapes.
deviations.impact: MEDIUM: clients expecting 404 for unknown ptyID will get 426 instead. While 426 is a "transient" error and clients should retry, it does not match the contract's error model. The 403 vs 426 distinction is also lost — clients can't distinguish "ticket invalid" from "WebSocket not implemented" without parsing the body.

missing_features: WebSocket upgrade (101 Switching Protocols) — the entire purpose of this endpoint
Ticket-based auth bypass in Loom's Authorization middleware (mirrors hasPtyConnectTicketURL from opencode)
PtyNotFoundError(404) handling on unknown ptyID
ForbiddenError(403) handling on invalid ticket
Custom query parameter parsing (location[directory], location[workspace], cursor, ticket)
Custom header parsing (x-opencode-ticket)
Pty.ID brand validation on path param
extra_features: None (the handler is a placeholder)
output.notes: Conformance level: NON_CONFORMANT. This endpoint has 3 deviations, all high/medium severity. The endpoint is the most complex of all PTY endpoints: WebSocket protocol upgrade + custom auth bypass + ticket validation + multiple error paths. The route comment at routes.rs:269-270 explicitly states the PTY handlers are "honest 501s until handlers/pty.rs ships the full lifecycle." The full implementation at apps/server/src/handlers/pty.rs includes the PTY WebSocket handling logic (pty.rs module docs), but is not wired. The 426 status code is technically semantically correct ("client should upgrade") but it does not actually upgrade — clients following the contract will hang. To make this endpoint work end-to-end, the wiring would need: (1) replace mcp_pty_file::get_api_pty_connect with the real handler, (2) add ticket-based auth bypass to Loom's Authorization middleware, (3) implement ForbiddenError and PtyNotFoundError shapes correctly. This is the largest single-endpoint implementation gap in the PTY group.

new_deviations_found.title: Config load failure returns 200 with empty array, not 503 ServiceUnavailableError
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: ServiceUnavailableError` (model.ts:13) with `{ message: Schema.String, service: Schema.optional(Schema.String) }` and `httpApiStatus: 503`. When the service cannot fulfill the request, server should return 503.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `bootstrap.rs:510-513`: `let cfg = match config::load_full_config(CONFIG_APP_NAME) { Ok(c) => c, Err(_) => return Vec::new(), };`. If config fails to load, `build_model_infos_with_models_dev` returns empty Vec. Handler at `bootstrap.rs:218-219` wraps this in `location_response(&state, Value::Array(models))` — produces 200 with `{location, data: []}`. No 503 path.
new_deviations_found.impact: Service unavailable (config can't load) is silently reported as an empty model list. Clients have no signal that the service is degraded. Boundary case — most clients will treat empty list as "no models available" rather than "service degraded." Severity medium.

new_deviations_found.title: No error handling for models.dev fetch failure
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: ServiceUnavailableError` (model.ts:13). Fetch failures should be reported as 503.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `bootstrap.rs:531`: `let entries = registry.list_all_models(&provider_configs).await;` — no `Result` handling. If `list_all_models` returns Err (network timeout, models.dev down), the behavior is implementation-dependent (panic or silently empty). No 503 mapping.
new_deviations_found.impact: Boundary case: when models.dev is unreachable, clients see either a 500 panic response or an empty 200 response. No graceful degradation or 503 propagation. Severity medium.

new_deviations_found.title: No fetch timeout for models.dev network call
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on fetch timeouts.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `registry.list_all_models(&provider_configs).await` at `bootstrap.rs:531` has no timeout. If models.dev is unresponsive, the handler blocks indefinitely.
new_deviations_found.impact: Potential DoS vector: a slow models.dev response blocks all model.list calls. Severity low (production deployments typically have network-level timeouts).

new_deviations_found.title: Extra `attachments` field in `capabilities` not in contract
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `Model.Capabilities = Schema.Struct({ tools: Schema.Boolean, input: Schema.Array(Schema.String), output: Schema.Array(Schema.String) })` (schema/model.ts:25-29). Three fields.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `bootstrap.rs:562-567`: emits `"capabilities": { tools, input, output, attachments }`. The `attachments` field is not in the contract's `Model.Capabilities` struct.
new_deviations_found.impact: Schema-strict clients reject the unknown `attachments` key. Permissive clients ignore it. Low severity.

new_deviations_found.title: Hardcoded `status: \"active\"`, `enabled: true`, `time.released: 0` — placeholder values not derived from spec
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Contract requires `Model.Info.status` (one of \"alpha\"|\"beta\"|\"deprecated\"|\"active\"), `enabled: Schema.Boolean`, `time.released: DateTimeUtcFromMillis`. Real values should come from spec data.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `bootstrap.rs:570-573`: hardcodes `\"time\": { \"released\": 0 }` (epoch 0 — January 1, 1970), `\"status\": \"active\"`, `\"enabled\": true`. The spec data is not consulted for these fields.
new_deviations_found.impact: Clients seeing `released: 0` display as 1970-01-01 — clearly wrong. All models shown as `status: active` regardless of true status. Behavior deviation, not strict schema violation (all values match contract types). Low severity.

new_deviations_found.title: Missing `family` field in Model.Info JSON
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `Model.Info` includes `family?: Model.Family` (optional, `Schema.String.pipe(Schema.brand(\"Family\"))`). Per schema/model.ts.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: The JSON construction at `bootstrap.rs:557-575` does not include a `family` field at all.
new_deviations_found.impact: Optional field, so absence is conformant with drop-on-encode convention. UIs that show model family (e.g., 'gpt-4', 'claude-3') won't get this. Low severity.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are mostly accurate. DEV-1 is partially confirmed — verified the JSON construction at `bootstrap.rs:557-575` shows several fields are placeholder values (`status: 'active'`, `enabled: true`, `time.released: 0`, `cost: []`, `variants: []`, `family` missing). Found 6 new boundary deviations. The auditor's `partial` classification is correct.

new_deviations_found.title: Whitespace-only sessionID/messageID accepted; no path validation
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `params: { sessionID: Session.ID, messageID: SessionMessage.ID }` where `Session.ID = Schema.String.check(Schema.isStartsWith(\"ses\"))` and `SessionMessage.ID = Schema.String.check(Schema.isStartsWith(\"msg_\"))` (`schema/session-id.ts`, `schema/session-message.ts`). Both brands enforce prefix.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `Path<(String, String)>` (`messages.rs:245`) — both plain strings. Any value accepted, including whitespace. Store lookup returns None for unknown ids, so 404.
new_deviations_found.impact: Wire-level conforms (brands don't round-trip). Boundary: whitespace-only IDs reach the handler and produce 404 instead of a 400 validation error. Already covered by DEV-4. Listed for completeness.

new_deviations_found.title: Cross-session message access prevented by data structure (keyed under session_id)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on cross-session isolation.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `messages.rs:247-252` does `state.messages.read().get(&session_id).and_then(|msgs| msgs.iter().find(|m| m.id == message_id))` — looks up the session FIRST, then iterates the session's messages. If session doesn't exist, returns None. If message doesn't belong to the session, not in the list.
new_deviations_found.impact: Cross-session message access is **prevented by the data structure** (messages are keyed under their session_id). No additional check needed. Listed as a confirmation that this defense-in-depth works correctly.

new_deviations_found.title: Two separate read locks held sequentially (state.messages then state.parts)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on lock semantics.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `messages.rs:247-265` acquires `state.messages.read()` first, releases it, then acquires `state.parts.read()`. Two sequential read locks with no atomicity guarantee between them.
new_deviations_found.impact: The two reads are not atomic: between releasing the messages lock and acquiring the parts lock, a `delete_api_session_message` could remove the message (and its parts). Handler would then return 404. Severity `low` (defensive; correct REST behavior).

new_deviations_found.title: Empty `parts` array returned for messages with no parts
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `Schema.Array(...)` (parts is part of `SessionMessage.Message` union, varies by variant). Empty arrays are valid.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler at `messages.rs:261` uses `unwrap_or_default()` to return empty Vec if no parts.
new_deviations_found.impact: Wire-conformant. Empty arrays are valid. No deviation.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: Behavioral expectation from opencode convention: a file read at a location should not allow reading files outside the location. Path normalization should resolve symlinks for the boundary check.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Path traversal protection should be canonical (filesystem-based), not just lexical. Symlinks within the location root should not allow escape.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `resolve_within` (fs.rs:66-86) does lexical normalization via the `normalize` helper (fs.rs:50-62) and checks `normalized.starts_with(root)` — both operations are pure string manipulation, no filesystem call. `location_root` canonicalizes (fs.rs:42-46), but the resolved path is NOT canonicalized before the boundary check or the read. A symlink inside the location root that points outside is silently followed.
new_deviations_found.title: Symlink-based path traversal — boundary check is lexical, not canonical
new_deviations_found.impact: A user (or attacker who can write to the location root, e.g. a project collaborator) can `ln -s /etc/passwd project/secrets` and then `GET /api/fs/read/secrets` to read `/etc/passwd` — `resolve_within` returns `Ok(...)` because the string starts with the root, but `std::fs::read` follows the symlink and reads the target. Real-world impact depends on threat model: for a single-user local Loom, this is mostly self-foot-shoot; for multi-tenant or untrusted-write scenarios, it's an escape.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:50-62 (`normalize` is lexical); fs.rs:66-86 (`resolve_within` does `normalized.starts_with(root)` without canonicalize); fs.rs:147 (`std::fs::read(&resolved)` follows symlinks).

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: Opencode convention typically caps file read sizes (e.g. 10MB max) to prevent memory exhaustion. The contract is silent on this.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `Schema.Uint8Array` success type — any size bytes is valid.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler calls `std::fs::read(&resolved)` (fs.rs:147) which loads the entire file into a `Vec<u8>`. No size check before or after the read. A request for a 10GB file allocates 10GB of RAM.
new_deviations_found.title: No file size limit — large files exhaust process memory (DoS vector)
new_deviations_found.impact: A single client can request `/api/fs/read/big_file.bin` (say, a multi-GB log or database dump) and crash the Loom process. Even a moderately large file (e.g. 1GB) can OOM the worker. No streaming — the entire payload sits in memory before being written to the response.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: HTTP/1.1 supports `Range`, `If-Modified-Since`, `If-None-Match`, `ETag`. Opencode convention typically uses ETag/Last-Modified for file reads to enable client caching.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: File read responses MAY support conditional GET (ETag/Last-Modified) and Range requests.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Response only sets `content-type: application/octet-stream` (fs.rs:159). No `etag`, no `last-modified`, no `content-length`, no `cache-control`. No `Range` parsing. Every request re-downloads the full file.
new_deviations_found.title: No ETag, Last-Modified, or Range support — every read re-downloads full content
new_deviations_found.impact: A client (e.g. TUI) that polls the same file repeatedly for change detection downloads the entire file each time. With a 1MB file polled every 5s, that's 720MB/hour of unnecessary I/O. Range requests for partial reads (e.g. tailing a log) are unsupported. Performance issue, not correctness.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: Behavioral expectation: reading a file that is being concurrently written should yield either the pre-write content or the post-write content, not a torn state.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Reads should be atomic at the file level.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler does (1) `std::fs::metadata(&resolved)` then (2) `std::fs::read(&resolved)`. Between these two calls, another process can truncate/rewrite the file. The metadata read sees the old inode; the read sees partial new content. Result: torn file content returned to client.
new_deviations_found.title: Torn reads on concurrent writes — metadata + read not atomic
new_deviations_found.impact: If another process (or another Loom handler, e.g. fs.write at fs.rs:226-257) truncates the file between `metadata` and `read`, the client receives partial/garbage content. For typical file-read workloads this is rare; for actively-written files (logs, sockets, journals) it's a real concern.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:129-156 (`std::fs::metadata` at :129, `std::fs::read` at :147 — two separate syscalls with no atomicity guarantee).

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: The contract path is `/api/fs/read/*` — empty path matches the wildcard and should yield a sensible response.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `GET /api/fs/read/` (empty path) should be handled.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler treats empty path as the location root. `resolve_within` normalizes to `root` (fs.rs:78). `metadata` succeeds (root is a dir), `is_dir()` returns true (fs.rs:140), returns 400 "path is a directory, not a file". Reasonable, but the contract might prefer a dedicated 404 or a specific "no path" error code.
new_deviations_found.title: `/api/fs/read/` (empty path) returns 400 "path is a directory" — works but opaque
new_deviations_found.impact: Minor: a client requesting the root directory without thinking sees a "directory" error rather than a clear "no path provided". Cosmetic; the 400 is the right status.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: Opencode convention: successful reads return binary content; clients rely on consistent content-type.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Binary files served as bytes — `application/octet-stream` is conformant.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Hardcoded `application/octet-stream` (fs.rs:159) regardless of actual file type. A `.txt` file is served as octet-stream; a `.html` file is also octet-stream. The contract's `Schema.Uint8Array` is type-agnostic, but a more useful behavior would be to set `Content-Type: text/plain` for text files, etc.
new_deviations_found.title: Content-Type is always `application/octet-stream` regardless of file extension
new_deviations_found.impact: Clients cannot rely on Content-Type to decide how to render the file. A TUI receiving a markdown file gets octet-stream and may not render it as text. Acceptable for binary-agnostic APIs but suboptimal for text-heavy workflows.

new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: The contract specifies a per-endpoint success type. Errors aren't declared, but the broader opencode convention uses TaggedErrorClass.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Errors should carry structured information (e.g. tag, requestedPath).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: All errors return `json!({"error": "<string>"})` — a single string with no structured fields. A 404 response has the same shape as a 403; the client must parse the HTTP status code AND read the error string to distinguish. The 400 "path is a directory" doesn't include the requested path; the 404 doesn't include the requested path; the 403 includes the requested path string in the message.
new_deviations_found.title: Error responses are inconsistent — 403 includes path, 400/404 don't; no structured error fields
new_deviations_found.impact: A v2 SDK client that builds a typed error model from the body will get a plain string, not a discriminated error. The 403 body has `"path 'foo' escapes location boundary"` (includes path), the 400 has `"path is a directory, not a file"` (no path), the 404 has the io::Error message (varies). Inconsistent shape makes error-handling code fragile.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:81-84 (403 with path), :131-138 (404/500 with io::Error message), :140-145 (400 without path), :147-156 (500 with io::Error message).

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's deviations are largely correct. DEV-1 (error body shape) is a real divergence from the broader opencode TaggedErrorClass convention — the contract itself doesn't declare errors for fs.read, so it's not a strict violation, but a v2 SDK doing tagged error matching will break. DEV-2 (named wildcard) is purely cosmetic, correctly classified as low. The conformance rating of `partial` is appropriate. From a behavior angle I found six additional issues the auditor missed — most importantly (1) symlink-based path traversal: `resolve_within` does lexical string normalization without canonicalization, so a symlink inside the location root that points outside is silently followed by `std::fs::read`. This is a real security boundary bypass. (2) No file size limit — `std::fs::read` loads the entire file into memory, a 10GB request OOMs the process. (3) No ETag/Last-Modified/Range support — every read re-downloads. (4) Torn reads on concurrent writes. (5) Inconsistent error body shape across status codes (403 includes path, 400/404 don't). (6) Hardcoded `application/octet-stream` regardless of file extension. The endpoint IS functionally correct for simple GET reads, has path-traversal protection (lexical), returns raw bytes with the right content-type, and applies auth middleware at router level. But the symlink gap is a real behavior issue that should be addressed.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED at medium. Re-read fs.ts:21-34 — the `HttpApiEndpoint.get("fs.read", "/api/fs/read/*", { query: LocationQuery, success: Schema.Uint8Array.pipe(HttpApiSchema.asUint8Array()) })` has NO `error: [...]` field. The contract is silent on error shape for fs.read specifically. However, the broader opencode convention (across all error-declaring endpoints) uses TaggedErrorClass with `_tag` discriminator, and a v2 SDK building a typed error model from response bodies will fail to match Loom's `{"error": "<string>"}` body. The auditor's classification of medium is defensible: it's not a strict contract violation but is a real divergence from convention that breaks SDK error handling. Severity medium is correct. Evidence verified: fs.rs:131-156 shows all error paths using `Json(json!({"error": ...}))` pattern.

At runtime both capture trailing path segments identically. The behavior is semantically equivalent; the difference is purely syntactic. Severity low is correct. Evidence verified.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are mostly accurate. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:596-659` and `apps/server/src/routes.rs:444-447` confirms: (a) DEV-1 (ServiceUnavailableError 503 never returned for busy sessions) is CONFIRMED — verified no busy-state check in handler; (b) DEV-2 (no real summarization, synthetic placeholder text) is CONFIRMED — `format!("Compacted {} prior session message(s).", messages.len())` at line 627; (c) DEV-3 (no Compaction message in state.messages) is CONFIRMED — only writes to `state.session_contexts`, no `state.messages` insert; (d) DEV-4 (stale docstring claims 501) is CONFIRMED — line 597-599 says "Returns 501 Not Implemented" but actual code returns `StatusCode::NO_CONTENT` at line 658; (e) DEV-5 (stale TODO comment at routes.rs:911) is CONFIRMED — endpoint IS wired at 444-447; (f) DEV-6 is REJECTED — false positive. The contract DOES define `session.next.context.updated` as a documented event (`packages/schema/src/session-event.ts:101-110`: `ContextUpdated = Event.define({ type: "session.next.context.updated", schema: { ...Base } })`). It's also in the event inventory (lines 454, 485). The auditor's claim that "Compaction namespace defines only Started, Delta, Ended — no context.updated event" is incorrect. Loom's emission of `session.next.context.updated` during compaction is actually contract-conformant. Severity `low` is moot because the event is conformant. Found 4 new findings: (1) `sessionLocationMiddleware` not applied (medium, same pattern as other session.* endpoints); (2) stale `session_contexts` entries on session deletion (low, memory hygiene); (3) `publish_durable` errors silently swallowed (low); (4) "Compacted 0 prior session message(s)" on empty sessions (low, defensive). The auditor's `partial` conformance classification is correct.

REJECTED — FALSE POSITIVE. The auditor claims `session.next.context.updated` is "not in the contract schema". Re-read `packages/schema/src/session-event.ts:101-110`: `export const ContextUpdated = Event.define({ type: "session.next.context.updated", ...options, schema: { ...Base } })`. This IS a documented event in the contract. It's also in the event inventory at lines 454 and 485. output.notes: Endpoint is wired and reachable (apps/server/src/routes.rs:481-482 → sse::api_session_event_stream in sse.rs:60-78). The SSE envelope shape matches the contract's Event.Payload: { id, type, data, durable?, location?, metadata? } with ids prefixed 'evt_v2_*' matching the Event.ID brand. Replay semantics work: replays durable events with seq > after, then streams live events filtered by aggregate_id, with a watermark to prevent event duplication. BUT a critical contract violation: no 404 SessionNotFoundError is ever returned for missing sessions — the handler just streams (potentially empty) without checking session existence. The contract's sessionLocationMiddleware (which performs the DB-backed session lookup) is not applied; Loom uses an inline aggregation filter that silently produces an empty stream for unknown sessions. Also missing brand validation on the sessionID path param.

side_effects.notes: Streaming and replay are implemented correctly: build_v2_session_stream (sse.rs:135-162) subscribes to the v2 event bus, captures a watermark before snapshot, replays durable events with seq > after AND seq <= watermark, then streams live events filtered by aggregate_id == session_id with seq > max(watermark, after). The watermark ensures events appear in exactly one of replay/live, never both. No state mutations on the server side beyond broadcast subscription. Persistence is via V2FileLog NDJSON files (v2_event.rs).

route_registration.notes: Route registered at apps/server/src/routes.rs:481-482 with path '/api/session/:sessionID/event' and GET method, wired to sse::api_session_event_stream. Path matches contract exactly (singular 'event', not 'events'). Real handler in apps/server/src/sse.rs. NOTE: stale TODO comment at routes.rs:909 lists this as TODO(W2) — should be cleaned up.

query_params.notes: Query<EventQuery> with after: Option<String> (sse.rs:80-84). Parsed as u64 with default '0' (sse.rs:65). Returns 400 bare text '`after` must be a non-negative u64' on parse failure (sse.rs:67-73). Path param sessionID extracted as Path<String> (sse.rs:62) with NO brand validation (contract requires Schema.String.check(isStartsWith('ses')).pipe(brand('SessionID'))). No LocationQuery (correct — contract doesn't require it). The aggregate_id filter in the stream subscription effectively substitutes for session existence validation but does not produce a 404.

payload_validation.notes: No payload (GET request). Query 'after' validated as u64. Path sessionID NOT validated for 'ses' prefix. No validation that the sessionID is well-formed.

error_handling.notes: CRITICAL: SessionNotFoundError (404) is declared in the contract (session.ts:333) but Loom NEVER returns it. The handler does not check whether the sessionID exists — it just subscribes to the v2 event bus and filters by aggregate_id. For an unknown session, the client receives a 200 OK with text/event-stream content-type and an empty stream. The contract explicitly states 'Errors are surfaced at stream-init time (first response), not mid-stream' (doc v2.session.events.md:100). Clients distinguishing 'session exists with no events yet' from 'session does not exist' will fail. 400 for invalid 'after' returns bare text '`after` must be a non-negative u64' (sse.rs:67-73) — not the contract's InvalidRequestError tagged body shape (though InvalidRequestError isn't declared for this endpoint either).

status_code.notes: 200 OK with text/event-stream content-type on success ✓. 400 on invalid 'after' (bare text). No 404 ever returned. No 401 (no auth middleware). No 500 (no obvious failure modes that would surface).

middleware.notes: Contract requires .middleware(sessionLocationMiddleware) which validates sessionID brand, performs DB-backed session lookup, and provides LocationServices. Loom does NOT apply this middleware. The handler takes Path<String> and Query<EventQuery> directly. No brand enforcement at route boundary. No DB-backed session validation.

response_shape.notes: SSE envelope shape matches the contract's Event.Payload: V2Event serializes to { id, type (renamed from event_type), data, durable?, location?, metadata? } (v2_event.rs:30-42). Event IDs are formatted 'evt_v2_{id}' (v2_event.rs), starting with 'evt_' matching the contract's Event.ID brand (schema/event.ts:9-12). SSE framing uses axum's Event::default().event('message').data(data) (sse.rs:164-169) — standard SSE. KeepAlive comments emitted every 10s. The 28-event SessionEvent.Durable union is dispatched via publish_durable calls throughout the codebase (e.g. session.rs:1312, 576, 112, etc.) — the shape is correct.

new_deviations_found.loom_does: `v2_compat::true_value` returns `Json(json!(true))` regardless of whether the `id` corresponds to a real saved permission. There is no store lookup or 404 path — Loom has no `PermissionSaved.Service.remove()` to call.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior gap (not a strict schema violation since contract declares no error class): clients cannot distinguish \"successfully removed\" from \"no such permission existed.\" REST DELETE conventionally allows either 204 (idempotent success) or 404 (not found) — Loom's behavior matches the idempotent interpretation but loses the audit trail. Severity `low` because the wire shape is conformant and REST DELETE idempotency is preserved.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate and well-evidenced. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/routes.rs:524-527` confirms the route registration `.get(handlers::v2_compat::empty_object).delete(handlers::v2_compat::true_value)`. The handler `true_value` at `apps/server/src/handlers/v2_compat.rs:22-24` is `pub async fn true_value() -> Json<Value> { Json(json!(true)) }` — returns 200 OK with body `true` (JSON literal, 4 bytes). All 5 deviations confirmed: (a) DEV-1 (200 vs 204) — `Json<Value>` defaults to 200 in axum, contract requires 204 NoContent; (b) DEV-2 (body `true` vs empty) — `json!(true)` produces non-empty body; (c) DEV-3 (no actual removal) — stub doesn't call any store/service; (d) DEV-4 (undeclared GET) — v2_compat::empty_object returns `{}` for an undeclared method; (e) DEV-5 (no brand check) — `Path<String>` accepts any string, `PermissionSaved.ID` brand has no `isStartsWith` constraint (just `Schema.brand(...)`). Severity classifications all correct. From a schema-conformance angle, the wire form is fundamentally wrong: status code 200 vs 204, body `true` vs empty, no Location.response envelope (correct for NoContent endpoint). The auditor's `non_conformant` classification is correct. Found 1 new finding (NEW-1): no 404 path for unknown id, but this is REST-conformant for idempotent DELETE (low severity). No SSE events emitted, no persistence concerns, idempotent, no race conditions.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/v2_compat.rs:22-24`: `pub async fn true_value() -> Json<Value> { Json(json!(true)) }`. In axum, `Json<T>` defaults to status 200 OK. The contract (`permission.ts:49-58`) declares `success: HttpApiSchema.NoContent` which is Effect's marker for HTTP 204 with empty body. Severity `high` is correct: clients expecting 204 (REST standard for DELETE) will see 200 instead. A v2 SDK client with `if (res.status === 204) {...}` branches will fall through to the wrong path.

CONFIRMED. Same code as DEV-1: `Json(json!(true))` produces body `true` (the 4-byte JSON literal). The contract's `HttpApiSchema.NoContent` requires an empty body. Severity `high` is correct: clients parsing JSON response will get `true` instead of empty/null. The body is non-empty when the contract requires empty.

CONFIRMED. `true_value` is a stub that always returns `true` without any state mutation, store lookup, or service call. Loom has no `PermissionSaved.Service.remove()` and no in-memory map for saved permissions. Severity `high` is correct: deleting a saved permission via this API is a no-op. Future requests matching the (non-removed) saved permission would still auto-approve. Once a real handler is wired (replacing `v2_compat::true_value` with one that calls a store), only DEV-1/DEV-2 (status code + body) would remain. The auditor's framing — \"full reference handler at opencode permission.ts:90-96 shows this is a 3-line handler — easy to implement when Loom gets PermissionSaved.Service\" — is accurate.

The brand `PermissionSaved.ID = Schema.String.pipe(Schema.brand(...))` (`schema/permission-saved.ts:8-12`) has NO `isStartsWith` constraint — just a brand and a `statics.create` helper that returns `\"psv_\" + ascending()`. So no `psv_` prefix validation is required at the wire level. Severity `low` is correct: brands don't round-trip; unknown ids just return 200 `{true}`.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's two deviations are correctly identified. Schema-conformance review of fs.read: (a) success type `Schema.Uint8Array.pipe(HttpApiSchema.asUint8Array())` correctly maps to raw bytes with `application/octet-stream` content-type (fs.rs:159-162); (b) NO `Location.response` envelope — raw bytes are returned directly, which matches the contract (no envelope for binary streams); (c) `LocationQuery` is accepted via first-class extractor (fs.rs:121) which functionally conforms to the contract's `query: LocationQuery`; (d) Path extraction via `Path<String>` from `*path` wildcard (routes.rs:261) — `axum` requires a name for the wildcard; the contract uses anonymous `*` for the same purpose; (e) Status codes: 200 OK on success, 404 on not-found, 403 on path-traversal, 400 on directory, 500 on IO error — all reasonable. (f) No payload, no declared errors, no brand constraints on path (RelativePath is wire-transparent at HTTP layer). (g) `Content-Length` is set automatically by axum when serving `Vec<u8>`. (h) No `Content-Disposition`, `ETag`, `Last-Modified`, or `Cache-Control` headers — none are contract-required. (i) The whole-file read into memory (`std::fs::read`, fs.rs:147) is a reasonable interpretation of `Schema.Uint8Array` (not a streaming interpretation) — schema-conformant but a potential DoS surface for very large files. From a STRICT schema-conformance angle, the endpoint is largely conformant; the deviations are real but minor.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: Verified. fs.rs:131-156 all error responses use `Json(json!({"error": "..."}))` — lowercase `error` field, no `_tag`, no class name. The contract at fs.ts:22-33 does NOT declare an `error: [...]` field on fs.read (only `success` and `query`), so the global TaggedErrorClass convention is technically not enforced by this endpoint's contract. The deviation is real vs the global convention but contract-not-declared for this specific endpoint. Severity "medium" is appropriate — clients using v2 SDK typed error handling will fall back to status-code parsing for fs.read errors.

Verified. routes.rs:261 — `.route("/api/fs/read/*path", get(handlers::fs::read))` — named wildcard. Contract at fs.ts:22 — `/api/fs/read/*` — anonymous wildcard. `axum` requires a name for wildcard captures (it does not support `*` without a name); the contract's `*` is effect-http notation. Functionally identical: both capture the trailing path segment(s). Severity "low" correct — purely cosmetic, no runtime difference. The handler uses `Path<String>` (fs.rs:122) which captures the named `*path` segment correctly.

new_deviations_found.impact: For files larger than available memory (multi-GB), the server OOMs. The contract's `Uint8Array` type doesn't specify streaming; Loom's whole-file load is one valid interpretation. Not a schema violation per se but a reliability concern. Flagged for completeness.

new_deviations_found.loom_does: fs.rs:147 — `let bytes = match std::fs::read(&resolved) { ... }` — loads the entire file into memory before responding. For a 10GB file, this allocates 10GB of memory in the handler.

new_deviations_found.impact: Path traversal protection works for lexical `..` escapes (fs.rs:50-86), but symlinks inside the location pointing OUTSIDE are NOT protected — `resolve_within` uses lexical `normalize`, not canonicalize. A file like `/project/sneaky_link` (symlink to `/etc/passwd`) inside the location would pass `resolve_within` and `std::fs::read` would follow the symlink. This is a SECURITY concern, not strictly a schema concern, but flag-worthy from a defense-in-depth perspective.
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `RelativePath` is a relative path string; the contract doesn't enforce lexical vs canonical semantics.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `resolve_within` uses `normalize` (fs.rs:50-62, lexical) rather than `canonicalize`. A symlink inside the location pointing outside passes the check; the OS-level `std::fs::read` follows it.

Polling loop with no event-driven wake; 100ms intervals and 5-minute timeout
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on implementation strategy. The contract says: \"Wait for a session agent loop to become idle\" — implementation strategy is unspecified.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `wait` handler at `session.rs:672-681` uses `tokio::time::timeout(timeout, async { loop { if lookup_run(...).is_none() { break; } sleep(100ms).await; } })` — pure polling at 100ms intervals with 5-minute timeout. No `Notify` or oneshot channel for event-driven wake.
new_deviations_found.impact: Performance: each `wait` request consumes server resources (timer wakeups, lock acquisitions) for up to 5 minutes. Under load (many concurrent waits), this could degrade server responsiveness. The contract doesn't require event-driven, but the polling design is suboptimal. Severity `medium` because the contract doesn't require a specific implementation strategy, so this is a \"Loom-internal design choice\" deviation, not a contract violation per se.

new_deviations_found.title: No way to cancel a wait via the HTTP request (server runs full 5 minutes)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on cancellation.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Once `wait` starts, the request thread blocks until either (a) the run becomes idle, or (b) the 5-minute timeout fires. No way for the client to cancel the wait (e.g., via dropped connection or explicit cancel endpoint). Axum's connection-drop detection may free the task, but the timeout will still tick down.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior: a client that loses interest in the wait (e.g., user closes the tab) still consumes server resources until the 5-minute timeout. Severity `low` (defensive optimization).

new_deviations_found.title: No SSE event emitted when wait completes (success or timeout)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract-declared event for session.wait.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Handler does not call `emit(&state, \"session.idle\", ...)` or similar. Subscribers to `/api/event` won't be notified when a session's agent loop becomes idle (this is exactly what they're likely waiting for).
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior gap: event-driven UIs must poll `session.wait` (or some other endpoint) to detect idle state. Severity `low` (no contract text mandates emission).

new_deviations_found.title: No idempotency token handling for retry safety
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on idempotency.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Each `wait` POST creates a new wait task. A client retrying after network failure will start a new wait that consumes additional resources. No idempotency key in the contract.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior gap: client retries can stack multiple concurrent waits. Severity `low` (REST POST convention typically allows non-idempotency, but wait endpoints are sensitive).

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/routes.rs:912` (TODO comment only, no `.route()` call) and `apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:664-683` (handler fully implemented but unreachable) confirms: (a) DEV-1 (route not registered, critical) — CONFIRMED. (b) DEV-2 (503 never produced on timeout, medium) — CONFIRMED. The `let _ = tokio::time::timeout(...)` (line 673) discards the timeout result; handler returns 204 regardless. (c) DEV-3 (no brand validation, low) — CONFIRMED. (d) DEV-4 (sessionLocationMiddleware not applied, medium) — CONFIRMED. The handler accepts `_loc: Query<LocationQuery>` (functional equivalent) but the route is not registered, so no router-level middleware exists. Behavior analysis: handler is read-only with no SSE events, no persistence concerns. The 5-minute timeout is silently swallowed. Multiple concurrent waits consume resources (no event-driven wake). The `not_implemented` conformance classification is correct. Found 4 new findings, all low-severity (design/implementation optimizations, not contract violations).

output.notes: Conformance level: CONFORMANT. The contract is explicit that this endpoint returns Location.Info DIRECTLY (not Location.response wrapped) — a rare exception to the usual wrapping pattern. Loom's handler at bootstrap.rs:55-63 returns Json(serde_json::to_value(LocationInfo::from_state(&state)).unwrap_or(Value::Null)) which produces the exact bare Location.Info shape: { directory: AbsolutePath, workspaceID?: WorkspaceID, project: { id: ProjectID, directory: AbsolutePath } }. The handler comment at line 59-61 explicitly documents this: "Contract (location.ts:29-42): GET /api/location returns bare Location.Info ... NOT wrapped in Location.response." Notably, this is one of only a few endpoints in the entire API where the response is NOT wrapped in Location.response. The other major exceptions are session.* endpoints (session.context, session.history, session.active, session.messages, session.message) which return bare { data } envelopes due to path-implicit location. Three Loom-specific extras (PATCH /api/location, PUT /api/location/workspace, GET /api/location/snapshot) are not in the v2 contract but are wired (workspace PUT is a v2_compat placeholder). These are not contract deviations — they are Loom extensions on top of the contract.

new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: SessionNotFoundError` (`session.ts:284`). Effect's `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` encodes as `{_tag: "SessionNotFoundError", sessionID, message}`. Standard contract pattern: all error responses are JSON objects.

The 404 case is particularly dangerous — its status code matches `SessionNotFoundError`, so clients checking only status may parse this as `SessionNotFoundError` and try to read JSON fields from a text body. output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/routes.rs:456-459` and `apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:1340-1379` confirms: (a) DEV-1 (409 "no revert is staged" with bare text body) — CONFIRMED at line 1348, severity `high` correct; (b) DEV-2 (404 "revert message not found" with bare text body) — CONFIRMED at line 1357, severity `high` correct (especially dangerous because 404 status matches `SessionNotFoundError`); (c) DEV-3 (stale TODO at routes.rs:919) — CONFIRMED, severity `low` correct; (d) DEV-4 (empty messageID silently tolerated) — CONFIRMED at line 1350, severity `low` correct. The `partial` conformance classification is correct. Schema analysis: success path returns `StatusCode::NO_CONTENT` (204 empty body) matching `HttpApiSchema.NoContent`; `SessionNotFoundError` body shape via `session_not_found` helper is `{_tag, sessionID, message}` matching `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` encoding; the `session.next.revert.committed` event payload `{timestamp, sessionID, messageID}` matches the contract's `RevertEvent.Committed` schema. Found 3 new findings: (1) `sessionLocationMiddleware` not applied (medium, similar to session.get); (2) ALL THREE revert routes have stale TODO comments (917, 918, 919) — auditor only flagged 919; (3) plain text response bodies for 409/404 instead of JSON error shapes (low, same issue as DEV-1/DEV-2 but from a wire-format angle). The endpoint is functionally correct but emits two undeclared error responses with non-conformant body shapes.

new_deviations_found.title: Pass-through projection does not validate `save`/`metadata`/`source` field types
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `Permission.Request` requires `save: Schema.Array(Schema.String)` (when present), `metadata: Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Unknown)` (when present), `source: Source` (when present, must be `{type: \"tool\", messageID, callID}`).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `to_contract_request` at `permission.rs:51-74` uses `req.input.get(\"save\").cloned()`, `.get(\"metadata\").cloned()`, `.get(\"source\").cloned()` — pure pass-through. If `save` is a string (not array), `metadata` is an array (not record), or `source.type` is `\"agent\"` (not `\"tool\"`), Loom emits the malformed value verbatim.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: a client storing a malformed permission request (e.g., via `POST /api/permission`) sees a downstream error when reading `GET /api/permission/request`. Schema-strict clients reject unknown types. Severity `low` because (a) the contract's trust boundary is at the call site (not the projection), (b) the input path is `post_api_permission` (v1 compat) which is similarly permissive, (c) the session-scoped `create_session_permission` validates `action` but not the optional fields.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/permission.rs:58-72 — `if let Some(save) = req.input.get(\"save\") { ... save.clone() };` (and similar for metadata, source).

new_deviations_found.title: No type validation on `sessionID` (empty string allowed)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `sessionID: SessionID` where `SessionID = Schema.String.check(Schema.isStartsWith(\"ses\")).pipe(...)` (`schema/session-id.ts`). Wire form accepts any string (brands don't round-trip), but the contract semantics require non-empty `ses_`-prefixed ids.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `to_contract_request` emits `req.session_id` verbatim. `post_api_permission` at `permission.rs:159-163` defaults `session_id` to `\"\"` when absent. So a permission request can be stored with empty `sessionID`.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: a permission request with `sessionID: \"\"` appears in the pending list with an empty session ID. Schema-strict clients can't associate the request with a real session. Severity `low` because (a) wire-level conforms (brands don't round-trip), (b) this is a v1 compat path (`post_api_permission`), not the v2 session-scoped path which validates.

new_deviations_found.title: Empty `action` string allowed
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `action: Schema.String` (required, any string).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `create_session_permission` at `permission.rs:299-303` defaults `req.tool` to `\"\"` when `action` is absent from the body. `to_contract_request` then emits `\"action\": \"\"`.
new_deviations_found.impact: Edge case: a permission request with empty `action` appears in the list with no description of what was requested. Schema-strict clients see `\"\"` and may treat it as malformed. Severity `low` because wire-level conforms (empty string is valid `Schema.String`).

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's `conformant` verdict is correct. Independent re-reading confirms: (a) the handler at `permission.rs:130-142` correctly wraps the result in `Location.response(...)` envelope matching `Location.response(Schema.Array(Permission.Request))`; (b) `to_contract_request` at `permission.rs:51-74` projects internal `PermissionRequest` (with `tool`/`input` fields) to the contract's `Permission.Request` shape (with `id`/`sessionID`/`action`/`resources`/`save?`/`metadata?`/`source?`); (c) all 4 required fields (`id`, `sessionID`, `action`, `resources`) are present with correct types; (d) all 3 optional fields (`save`, `metadata`, `source`) are correctly omitted when absent (per the contract's drop-on-encode `optional()` helper); (e) `id` format is `per_`-prefixed via `new_permission_id()` matching the contract's `ID = Schema.String.check(Schema.isStartsWith(\"per\"))`; (f) `resources` defaults to empty array `[]` (valid `Schema.Array(Schema.String)`); (g) status filter (`req.status == \"pending\"`) matches the contract's \"List pending permission requests\" description. No new schema deviations found beyond minor edge cases at the v1-compat input paths. Found 3 low-severity edge cases: (1) pass-through projection doesn't validate `save`/`metadata`/`source` types; (2) empty `sessionID` allowed from v1-compat path; (3) empty `action` allowed from session-scoped create. output.notes: POST /api/session/:sessionID/interrupt is registered, returns 204 NoContent on the happy path (matches HttpApiSchema.NoContent). Route path and HTTP method match the contract exactly, handler is real (not v2_compat), global auth middleware is applied, and the session.status event payload { sessionID, status: { type: "idle" } } matches the contract's SessionStatusEvent.Status schema. CRITICAL deviation: the contract declares SessionNotFoundError for this endpoint (session.ts:348), but the handler NEVER returns it. The handler calls session_abort and discards its return value with let _ = ..., then unconditionally returns StatusCode::NO_CONTENT. session_abort itself does not check whether the session exists — it only checks lookup_run (which returns the run token, not the session record). For a non-existent session: lookup_run returns None, no abort happens, but a session.status event is STILL emitted for the non-existent session (silent state pollution). Clients implementing against the contract expecting 404 on missing sessions will silently receive 204 and believe the interrupt succeeded. This is a fundamental error-handling failure, not a cosmetic issue.

side_effects.notes: Calls session_abort which: (1) cancels the active run token via lookup_run + token.cancel(); (2) ends the run; (3) emits a session.status event with payload { sessionID, status: { type: "idle" } } — matches SessionStatusEvent.Status schema (session-status-event.ts:35-41). Idempotent: calling interrupt on an idle session is a no-op (just emits an idle status event). Atomic: cancel + end_run are guarded by separate locks but the run token generation check prevents races. Side effect concern: emits session.status event even for non-existent sessions (DEV-1 root cause) — this pollutes the SSE bus with events for sessions that don't exist.

Refresh_expiry is called during the read path, transitioning `pending` → `expired` (mild GET-with-side-effect, but idempotent). Lock usage is correct (write lock acquired, lookup + clone + release, then `location_response` outside the lock). Concurrent GET + DELETE are race-free. No auth bypass, no state leakage, no timeout concerns. Found 5 additional latent behavior deviations (would surface if W2 wires the route): handler-specific 404 body shape, no SSE event on status transitions, no persistence (static `OnceLock<RwLock<HashMap>>`), `refresh_expiry` side effect, and missing `attemptID` brand validation + discarded `LocationQuery`. In `find_entries` (fs.rs:485-486): `let want_files = kind_filter.map(|k| k == \"file\").unwrap_or(true); let want_dirs = kind_filter.map(|k| k == \"directory\").unwrap_or(true);`. With `kind_filter = Some(\"foo\")`, both `want_files` and `want_dirs` evaluate to false. The function returns empty results. Client sees 200 with `data: []` — no error. Same for `type=` (empty string) and `type=File` (case mismatch).
new_deviations_found.impact: Validation gap: contract's literal union is enforced only by string comparison, not by validation. Clients sending `type=files` (typo) get empty results rather than a clear 400 error. UX is degraded but not data-corrupting.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:435-436 — `kind: Option<String>` with rename=\"type\" but no `Schema.Literals` validator; fs.rs:485-486 — accepts any string and uses `.map(... == \"file\")` matching.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate and well-evidenced from a boundary perspective. Independent re-reading of the contract (`packages/protocol/src/groups/fs.ts:13-18, 49-62`), the schema (`packages/schema/src/filesystem.ts:14-40`), the handler (`apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:425-567`), and the route (`apps/server/src/routes.rs:262`) confirms both DEV-1 (handler-specific 400 body shape) and DEV-2 (Loom stricter than contract: whitespace-only rejection, default limit=200). Boundary analysis: empty/whitespace query → 400 ✓; missing query → 400 ✓; invalid `type` value → silently empty (NEW-1); `limit=0` → silently empty (NEW-2); `limit=u64::MAX` → no upper cap (NEW-3); depth limit 10 (defensive, undocumented); hidden file filtering (defensive); silent I/O error swallowing (NEW-5); stale TODO comment in routes.rs (NEW-4); concurrent access — pure read, no race conditions; symlink handling follows OS default; encoding is lossy (`String::from_utf8_lossy`). reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED. output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are partially correct. Verified: (a) DEV-1 (loose payload validation) is CONFIRMED — `session.rs:492-494` accepts any string and silently keeps existing agent when `agent` is missing/null/non-string. However, the severity `low` is **under-classified** — the contract requires `agent` to be a REQUIRED field (`payload: Schema.Struct({ agent: Agent.ID })`), and Loom treats it as optional. This is a contract-conforming validation gap with severity `medium` (NEW-2 separates this from the brand check). Found 4 additional deviations: (1) `sessionLocationMiddleware` not applied — handler has no `Query<LocationQuery>` extractor and route has no `.layer(...)` (NEW-1, medium); (2) missing `agent` field silently keeps existing instead of returning 400 (NEW-2, medium — severity should be promoted from DEV-1's `low`); (3) empty `agent` string accepted (NEW-3, low); (4) function name `api_session_prompt` doesn't match the contract's `session.switchAgent` identifier (NEW-4, informational, code quality). Schema analysis: response is correctly `HttpApiSchema.NoContent` (204 empty body); `SessionNotFoundError` correctly returned on unknown session; `path sessionID: Session.ID` wire-conformant (no prefix required). The auditor's `partial` conformance classification is correct.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED with severity **upgrade** from `low` to `medium`. The auditor's framing is correct (loose validation: `body.get(\"agent\").and_then(Value::as_str)` accepts any string and silently skips if absent), but the severity understates the impact. The contract's `payload: Schema.Struct({ agent: Agent.ID })` (`session.ts:175`) declares `agent` as REQUIRED (no `optional()` wrapper). This is a contract-conforming validation gap, not just a \"loose brand check.\" The brand issue (Agent.ID is just a brand with no `isStartsWith`) is separate and not really a deviation — wire-level conforms for any string. The `#[serde(rename = \"type\")]` attribute causes serde_json to serialize the `kind` Rust field as the JSON key `\"type\"`. The wire output is `{\"path\": \"...\", \"type\": \"file\"}` — which EXACTLY matches the contract's `FileSystem.Entry = { path: RelativePath, type: Schema.Literals([\"file\", \"directory\"]) }` (`packages/schema/src/filesystem.ts:14-18`). output.overall_assessment: The auditor's CONFORMANT verdict is **incorrect**. The auditor claimed "server.connected is auto-emitted on stream open (sse.rs:102-108)" — this is factually wrong. sse.rs:102-108 is inside `build_stream`, which is used by the v1 `/global/event` endpoint. The v2 `/api/event` endpoint uses `build_v2_stream` (sse.rs:127-133), which does NOT emit `server.connected` — it only forwards V2Events from the broadcast bus. The contract's `schema()` helper (event.ts:18-26) explicitly auto-injects `server.connected` into the union when ServerDefinitions doesn't already include it, so v2 SDK clients expecting the "stream is alive" handshake will block forever. Beyond this critical error, I found seven additional behavior-angle issues: V2Event.location is never populated (always null); V2Event.data is untyped (no per-event-type schema validation); broadcast channel overflow silently drops events; serialization failures silently drop events; V2Event.id format diverges from the contract (`evt_v2_<seq>` vs `evt_<ascending>`); IDs reset on restart (not globally unique); no Last-Event-ID resume support on the global stream. The handler IS real (not a placeholder), the route IS registered, the auth middleware DOES apply, the SSE framing IS correct (`event: message` + JSON data), and v1 vs v2 buses are properly separated. But the missing `server.connected` alone breaks the v2 SDK's stream-readiness handshake.

new_deviations_found.title: Cursor encoding is incorrect: emits page SIZE not current OFFSET
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Cursors are opaque (`message.ts:19-21`). The exact format is not specified, but the semantics must be: pass cursor back to get the NEXT page. The cursor must encode the position from which to continue.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `let next_cursor = if has_more { Some(limit.to_string()) } else { None };` (`messages.rs:163-167`). The cursor is `limit.to_string()` — the page SIZE (e.g. "50" for limit=50), not the current OFFSET (which would be the index of the last item returned + 1). For a session with 100 messages and limit=50: first response has `cursor.next = \"50\"`, but the next page should start at offset 50 (returning items 51-100). The emitted value happens to be 50 numerically, but only because limit equals the page size. If the client passes a different limit on subsequent requests, the cursor would be wrong even if consumed.
new_deviations_found.impact: HIGH (compounded with NEW-1): even if the cursor were consumed, the encoding is wrong. A client paginating with limit=50 and then re-paginating with limit=20 would receive items starting at offset 50 (skipping 30 items). This is a fundamental pagination bug.

new_deviations_found.title: `UnknownError` (500) never returned on serialization failures
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: [InvalidCursorError, SessionNotFoundError, UnknownError]` (`message.ts:36`). `UnknownError` should map to 500 on unexpected serialization errors.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `serde_json::to_value(message).unwrap_or(Value::Null)` (`messages.rs:111`) silently substitutes `null` on serialization failure rather than returning 500.
new_deviations_found.impact: Real projection bugs become silent `null` messages. Low severity because `MessageInfo` is unlikely to fail serialization in practice.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are partially correct. Verified: (a) DEV-1 (response items `{info, parts}`) is CONFIRMED at `messages.rs:110-114` and `:155-159` — high severity wire-form deviation; (b) DEV-2 (404 body `_tag` vs `name`) is **PARTIALLY REJECTED** — the contract's `SessionNotFoundError` is `Schema.TaggedErrorClass<...>(\"SessionNotFoundError\", ...)` (`errors.ts:55-62`), which Effect encodes as `{_tag: \"SessionNotFoundError\", ...}` — so the auditor's claim that the contract uses `name` is INCORRECT. Loom's `{_tag, sessionID, message}` matches the Effect convention exactly. The `InvalidCursorError` and `UnknownError` gaps are real, though; (c) DEV-3 (cursor.previous null, default limit 50) is CONFIRMED; (d) DEV-4 (no brand check) is CONFIRMED. Found 6 NEW behavior deviations, including **two HIGH-severity pagination bugs**: (1) cursor is generated but NEVER consumed (`query.cursor` is destructured but never referenced in the handler body — pagination is broken end-to-end), (2) cursor encoding is `limit.to_string()` (page SIZE) instead of the current offset. Other findings: `limit` silently clamped to 200 (medium), `order` value not validated against literal union (low), `order + cursor` combination silently accepted (medium — contract explicitly forbids), `UnknownError` (500) never returned on serialization failures (low). The endpoint has a fundamentally broken pagination mechanism — even if the cursor were consumed, the encoding logic would still be wrong.

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:100-114` (`project_message`) and `:155-159` (used in handler body). Each data item is `{info: <MessageInfo JSON>, parts: [Value]}` — NOT the contract's flat `SessionMessage.Message` (tagged union by `type` with 8 variants: agent-switched, model-switched, user, synthetic, system, shell, assistant, compaction — `schema/session-message.ts:48-59`). The handler's own doc comment at `messages.rs:97-99` admits: \"Project a stored MessageInfo + its parts into the SessionMessage.Message shape. Returns `{info, parts}` — a reasonable projection of the tagged union until a full SessionMessage.Message type is implemented.\" Severity `high` is correct. v2 SDK clients expecting SessionMessage.Message will fail to parse — there's no `type` discriminator field on the items at all.

PARTIALLY REJECTED. Two sub-claims: (1) \"404 body uses _tag instead of name\" — **REJECTED**. Re-read `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts:55-62`: `class SessionNotFoundError extends Schema.TaggedErrorClass<SessionNotFoundError>()(\"SessionNotFoundError\", { sessionID: Schema.String, message: Schema.String }, { httpApiStatus: 404 }) {}`. Effect's `Schema.TaggedErrorClass` encodes as `{_tag: \"SessionNotFoundError\", sessionID, message}` — NOT `name`. Loom's response body at `messages.rs:129-134` is `{_tag: \"SessionNotFoundError\", sessionID, message}` which MATCHES the contract exactly. The auditor's claim that the contract uses `name` is incorrect. (2) \"InvalidCursorError never returned\" — **CONFIRMED**. The contract declares `error: [InvalidCursorError, SessionNotFoundError, UnknownError]` (`message.ts:36`); Loom never produces `InvalidCursorError` (NEW-5 confirms). Severity `medium` is justified for the InvalidCursorError/UnknownError gap but not for the `_tag` vs `name` issue.

CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:152, 163-167, 172`. (a) `query.limit.unwrap_or(50).min(200)` — default 50, max 200. (b) `Some(limit.to_string())` — cursor encoding is offset (page size). (c) `previous: Value::Null` (line 172) — always null. All three sub-claims verified. Note: I found an ADDITIONAL bug: the cursor is GENERATED but NEVER CONSUMED (NEW-1) — the handler ignores `query.cursor` entirely. So even if the cursor were honored, pagination is broken because the encoding is wrong (NEW-2). Severity `medium` is correct, but the actual functional impact is much worse than described.

CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/messages.rs:121`: `Path(session_id): Path<String>` — plain string. Contract says `params: { sessionID: Session.ID }` where `Session.ID = Schema.String.check(Schema.isStartsWith(\"ses\")).pipe(Schema.brand(\"Session.ID\"))` (`schema/session-id.ts`). Loom accepts any string. Wire-level conforms (brands don't round-trip). Severity `low` correct: 404 is returned for unknown ids, so the practical impact is just the error code (404 instead of 400).

new_deviations_found.contract_says: `HttpApiGroup.make(\"server.permission\")...add(permission.saved.remove).middleware(locationMiddleware)` (`permission.ts:48-61`). The `permission.saved.remove` endpoint is added BEFORE `.middleware(locationMiddleware)`, so the middleware should apply to it.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `/api/permission/saved/:id` is registered as `.get(...).delete(...)` (`routes.rs:524-527`) with no `.layer(...)` for any middleware. The handler `v2_compat::true_value` takes no extractors at all.

Since the handler doesn't read state, the missing middleware has no observable effect on the response (the response is hardcoded `true`). Severity `low` because no client can detect the missing middleware from the wire response. The deviation would matter if/when the handler is replaced with a real implementation.

new_deviations_found.title: Stub is idempotent in a degenerate way — always returns success regardless of id validity
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Standard REST DELETE should be idempotent (same result on repeated calls) and return 204 No Content on success. No explicit text on whether 404 should be returned for unknown ids.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `v2_compat::true_value` always returns `Json(json!(true))` (200 OK with body `true`) regardless of the id's validity. No 404 path. No actual removal performed.
new_deviations_found.impact: Idempotent in the wrong way — every call returns the same 200 + `true`, but the resource isn't actually removed. If a client retries DELETE on an unknown id, no error is returned (which is REST-conformant for DELETE), but the success is fake. Severity `low` because idempotency semantics for DELETE are intentionally permissive.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's 5 deviations are all confirmed. Independent re-reading of `packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts:48-58` (contract), `apps/server/src/handlers/v2_compat.rs:22-24` (`true_value`), and `apps/server/src/routes.rs:524-527` (route registration) confirms: (a) `true_value` returns `Json(json!(true))` — body is the JSON literal `true`, status 200; (b) contract requires `HttpApiSchema.NoContent` (204 with empty body); (c) DELETE registered with `.delete(v2_compat::true_value)` — no actual removal logic; (d) GET also registered via `.get(v2_compat::empty_object)` — undeclared in contract; (e) path param is plain `String` (no brand check on `psv_` prefix). All severity classifications (DEV-1/DEV-2/DEV-3 high, DEV-4/DEV-5 low) are correct. The `non_conformant` classification is correct — the endpoint fundamentally doesn't conform to contract (wrong status code, wrong body shape, no actual work done). Found 3 additional low-severity findings: `locationMiddleware` not applied (group-level middleware expected per `permission.ts:60-61`), no SSE event would be emitted on (would-be) removal, and the stub is idempotent in a degenerate way (always returns success, never performs work).

Cross-checked `packages/protocol/src/groups/permission.ts:48-58`: contract declares `success: HttpApiSchema.NoContent` which is 204 with empty body. Status code deviation is real and high-severity. new_deviations_found.title: LocationQuery is ignored on `location.get`; server always returns its default project
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `query: LocationQuery` (`location.ts:31`). The endpoint description says "Resolve the requested location or the server default location" (`location.ts:39`). A client sending `?location[directory]=otherdir&location[workspace]=wrk_1` expects the response to reflect that requested location (or a clear 404 if not resolvable).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `get_api_location` at `bootstrap.rs:55-63` destructures `Query(_loc): Query<LocationQuery>` and **discards** the parsed query. The handler always returns `LocationInfo::from_state(&state)` — the server's current default project. The query is parsed for conformance but never consulted. Compare to sibling handlers: `fs.list` (`fs.rs:184-216`) uses `location_root(&state, &q.location)` to resolve the requested directory; `fs.read` uses `loc.resolve_directory(&state)` similarly. `location.get` does NOT consult the query at all.
new_deviations_found.impact: Behavior gap: a v2 SDK client sending `?location[directory]=otherdir` expects the response's `directory`, `workspaceID`, and `project.{id,directory}` fields to reflect `otherdir`. Loom always returns the server default project regardless. If the server has only one project (typical Loom deployment), the response is identical for every query — making the parameter functionally dead. If multi-location support is ever added, this handler will silently return wrong results. Severity `medium` because (a) the query is part of the contract's public surface, (b) the contract description explicitly says \"resolve the requested location\", (c) other handlers in the same codebase honor the query — so this is an inconsistency, not a contract-conforming design choice.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/bootstrap.rs:55-63 — handler signature `Query(_loc): Query<LocationQuery>` then `Json(serde_json::to_value(LocationInfo::from_state(&state)).unwrap_or(Value::Null))`. The parsed `_loc` is never read. Compare to `apps/server/src/handlers/fs.rs:184-216` (`fs.list`) which calls `location_root(&state, &q.location)` to resolve the directory.
new_deviations_found.evidence_contract: C:/Users/heycj/dev/opencode/packages/protocol/src/groups/location.ts:31, 39 — `query: LocationQuery` and description `Resolve the requested location or the server default location`.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's `conformant` verdict on the wire-shape question is correct — the GET response exactly matches the contract's `Location.Info` shape (bare, not wrapped in `Location.response`), with correct field names and types. The handler comment at `bootstrap.rs:59-62` explicitly documents this contract exception. However, the auditor missed a real behavior gap: **`LocationQuery` is ignored**. The contract declares `query: LocationQuery` and the endpoint description says \"Resolve the requested location or the server default location\" — implying the query SHOULD be consulted. Loom's handler at `bootstrap.rs:55-63` destructures the query as `_loc` and discards it, always returning `LocationInfo::from_state(&state)` (the server default). Compare to sibling handlers (`fs.list`, `fs.read`) which DO honor the query via `location_root(&state, &q.location)`. This is a real deviation with `medium` severity. Other findings: (a) PATCH /api/location mutates state without emitting SSE event (low); (b) PATCH persistence is in-memory only, contradicting module doc's \"persist\" wording (low); (c) PATCH itself is not in v2 contract but is informational only for the GET audit. From a pure wire-shape angle, the auditor is correct. From a behavior angle, there's a real query-ignored gap.

The auditor's verdict of "CONFORMANT, 0 deviations" is INCORRECT. Re-reading the code reveals at least two significant boundary deviations the auditor missed entirely. The most critical: the contract schema **explicitly auto-injects `server.connected`** (event.ts:18-26 — the `Schema.Union` conditionally adds it when not in `EventManifest.ServerDefinitions`), but Loom's v2 stream at `build_v2_stream` (sse.rs:127-133) does NOT emit this initial event. The auditor cited sse.rs:102-108 as evidence that server.connected IS emitted on stream open, but those lines are inside `build_stream` (the v1 path called by `event_stream` at line 47); the v2 handler `api_event_stream` (line 52-57) takes a completely different code path via `build_v2_stream`, which subscribes to v2_event_tx and forwards events without any seed or heartbeat. A v2 client subscribing to `/api/event` receives ZERO initial events and ZERO connection-lifecycle signals until a real workload event is published — which may never happen. This breaks any client that expects a server.connected handshake. Additionally, `server.heartbeat` (which the v1 path emits every 10s at lines 113-120) is also missing from the v2 stream. The auditor's verdict is wrong; the endpoint is partial.

The two streams are completely separate code paths.

Lines sse.rs:102-108 are inside the `build_stream` function (V1 path used by `event_stream` / `/global/event`), NOT inside `build_v2_stream` (V2 path used by `api_event_stream` / `/api/event`). new_deviations_found.title: `admittedSeq` is computed BEFORE the user message is appended; semantics depend on interpretation
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `Admitted.admittedSeq: NonNegativeInt` (`schema/session-input.ts:16`). Sequence number indicating the position at which the message was admitted. Contract does not explicitly specify whether `admittedSeq` is the position before or after insertion.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `prompt_v2` at `session.rs:242-247`: `let admitted_seq = state.messages.read().get(&session_id).map(|m| m.len() as u64).unwrap_or(0);` — computed BEFORE the new user message is appended (line 289 does the append). So if the array was empty, `admittedSeq = 0` and the message ends up at position 0. If the array had 5 messages, `admittedSeq = 5` and the message ends up at position 5.
new_deviations_found.impact: Schema-conformant at the wire level (`NonNegativeInt` accepts the value). Semantic interpretation depends on the client. The natural reading is \"admittedSeq = the index at which the message was inserted.\" Loom's behavior is consistent with this. Severity `low` (informational; not a wire-form deviation).
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:242-247 (admittedSeq computation), :284-289 (append happens AFTER admittedSeq is captured).

new_deviations_found.title: `delivery` field case-sensitive; \"Queue\"/\"STEER\" silently rejected as \"queue\"
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `SessionInput.Delivery = SessionDelivery.Delivery = Schema.Literals([\"steer\", \"queue\"])` (`schema/session-delivery.ts`). Schema.Literals is case-sensitive.

new_deviations_found.title: `invalid_request` 400 body shape does NOT match `InvalidRequestError` contract shape (missing `_tag`, `kind`)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: InvalidRequestError` (`packages/protocol/src/groups/integration.ts:102`). The `InvalidRequestError` class (`packages/protocol/src/errors.ts:3-11`) extends `Schema.TaggedErrorClass(\"InvalidRequestError\", ...)` with payload `{message, kind?: string, field?: string}` and `httpApiStatus: 400`. The `kind` field enables OAuth-specific error categorization (e.g., `\"integration_authorization\"` vs `\"integration_code_required\"`).
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `integration.rs:447-454` defines `fn invalid_request(message: &str, field: Option<&str>)` returning `(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, Json(json!({\"error\": {\"message\": message, \"field\": field}})))`. The shape is `{error: {message, field?}}` — NO `_tag` discriminator, NO `kind` field. Used at `integration.rs:410-413` (non-pending attempt) and `:422-425` (no provider).
new_deviations_found.impact: If the route were wired, clients receiving a 400 would get a body without `_tag: \"InvalidRequestError\"` and without `kind`. A v2 SDK client doing `error._tag === \"InvalidRequestError\"` matching or `error.kind === \"integration_authorization\"` would fail. The `kind` discriminator is specifically important for OAuth because clients use it to decide retry behavior. Severity medium because this is a structural divergence that would surface as soon as the route is wired.
new_deviations_found.evidence_loom: apps/server/src/handlers/integration.rs:447-454 — `fn invalid_request(message: &str, field: Option<&str>)` returns `{error: {message, field?}}` shape, no `kind` field.

It does NOT call `crate::v2_event::publish_live` or `publish_durable`.

Only v1 clients subscribing to `/global/event` see the event. The contract's `Session.interrupt` description says \"Interrupt active execution owned by this OpenCode process. Idle interruption is a no-op.\" — v2 clients expect to observe interruption via the `session.status` event but receive nothing. Severity `critical` because v2 SDK session lifecycle management is broken.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate and well-evidenced. Independent re-reading of the contract (`packages/protocol/src/groups/credential.ts`, `packages/schema/src/credential.ts`, `packages/protocol/src/errors.ts`), the Loom handler (`apps/server/src/handlers/credential.rs:73-95`), the route registration (`apps/server/src/routes.rs:211-215`), and the state store (`apps/server/src/state.rs:633-680`) confirms both DEV-1 (404 body shape) and DEV-2 (no persistence). The handler is honest about its limitations — module docs explicitly note "Cross-restart persistence of credentials is therefore not wired here" — and follows the project rule of "real behavior or explicit 501" by returning 404 instead of a success-shaped stub for unknown ids. Boundary analysis: empty/missing payload → 400 (axum default, not `InvalidRequestError` shape); unknown/non-prefixed id → 404; concurrent PATCH + DELETE → last-write-wins via parking_lot write lock; lock released before response construction (no lock leak); no TOCTOU vulnerability; SSE event not emitted (no contract event declared). Found 4 new low-severity boundary deviations: payload-validation error shape, missing SSE event, ignored `LocationQuery`, and missing `cred_` brand validation. The `partial` conformance classification is correct.
