new_deviations_found.title: Forward-looking: Error body wraps `InvalidRequestError` in `{error: ...}` and omits `_tag` discriminator
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `error: InvalidRequestError` (`integration.ts:49`) where `InvalidRequestError = Schema.TaggedErrorClass<...>(\"InvalidRequestError\", { message: Schema.String, kind: optional(Schema.String), field: optional(Schema.String) }, { httpApiStatus: 400 })` (`errors.ts:3-11`). Effect's `TaggedErrorClass` adds a `_tag: \"InvalidRequestError\"` discriminator on the wire. The body should be flat: `{_tag, message, kind?, field?}`.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: The `invalid_request` helper at `integration.rs:448-454` constructs `(StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST, Json(json!({ \"error\": { \"message\": ..., \"field\": ... } })))` — the body is nested in an outer `error` key (not flat) and missing the `_tag` discriminator. If `connect_key` returns `Err(invalid_request(\"key is required\", Some(\"key\")))` at line 263, the wire body is `{\"error\": {\"message\": \"key is required\", \"field\": \"key\"}}` instead of the contract's `{\"_tag\": \"InvalidRequestError\", \"message\": \"key is required\", \"field\": \"key\"}`.
new_deviations_found.impact: Schema deviation in error path: (1) extra `error` wrapper key, (2) missing `_tag` discriminator. v2 SDK clients that switch on `body._tag === \"InvalidRequestError\"` will fail to recognize this error and may treat it as a generic 400. new_deviations_found.impact: HIGH (functional break): the contract's semantic is \"active sessions = keys present in map.\" Loom's response includes both busy and idle. A v2 SDK client cannot determine activity status from Loom's response. To fix correctly, Loom needs `filter(|s| lookup_run(...).is_some())` before mapping. This is a separate functional issue from the envelope shape (DEV-1) and value shape (DEV-2).

new_deviations_found.title: Empty-string defaults for missing `modelID`/`providerID` may not match contract
new_deviations_found.contract_says: Contract requires `Session.ID` keys (branded strings). It doesn't constrain values directly, but values are `SessionActive = { type: \"running\" }` per the contract. Loom's extra fields (`modelID`, `providerID`, etc.) are NOT in the contract, so they're not validated.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `v2_compat.rs:95-96`: `session.model.as_ref().map(...).unwrap_or_default()` — if `session.model` is `None`, emits `\"\"` (empty string) for both `modelID` and `providerID`. Likewise `agent` defaults to `\"build\"` via `unwrap_or_else`.
new_deviations_found.impact: Loom-specific extras, not contract-relevant. Severity `low` because (a) these fields are not in the contract's `SessionActive`, (b) clients ignoring the extras won't care, (c) clients reading them might see unexpected empties.

new_deviations_found.title: `lookup_run` called per session inside iterator (N+1 lock acquisitions)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on performance.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: `active_sessions` at `v2_compat.rs:94` calls `crate::state::lookup_run(&state, &session.id).is_some()` for each session. `lookup_run` likely acquires a read lock on `state.runs` (need to verify). With N sessions, this means N+1 lock acquisitions per response.
new_deviations_found.impact: Performance, not correctness. Severity `low` because (a) the endpoint is not high-throughput, (b) parking_lot's read lock is fast, (c) concurrent callers are serialized briefly.

new_deviations_found.title: Extra fields not in `SessionActive` (modelID, providerID, agent, startedAt, updatedAt)
new_deviations_found.contract_says: `SessionActive = Schema.Struct({ type: Schema.Literal(\"running\") })` — exactly one field.
new_deviations_found.loom_does: Loom emits 7 fields per item: `id`, `state`, `modelID`, `providerID`, `agent`, `startedAt`, `updatedAt`. Six of these are not in the contract's `SessionActive`.
new_deviations_found.impact: Schema-strict clients rejecting unknown keys would fail. Permissive clients ignore extras. Severity `low` (extra fields, not missing required ones).

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate and well-evidenced. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/routes.rs:485-487` (route) and `apps/server/src/handlers/v2_compat.rs:87-103` (handler) confirms: (a) route is wired to `handlers::v2_compat::active_sessions` — a real handler (not a v2_compat empty stub); (b) handler returns `Json(json!({\"sessions\": sessions}))` where `sessions` is a JSON array of rich objects — fundamentally different from the contract's `Schema.Struct({ data: Schema.Record(Session.ID, SessionActive) })` which requires a JSON object keyed by SessionID with `{type: \"running\"}` values; (c) Loom's `state` field uses `\"busy\"|\"idle\"` two-value enum, not the contract's single-value literal `\"running\"`. Severity `high` for DEV-1 (envelope shape fundamentally different) and `medium` for DEV-2 (value shape different) are correct. The `non_conformant` classification is correct. Found 4 additional boundary deviations, including **NEW-1 (high severity)**: idle sessions are included in the response, but the contract's design says \"Sessions absent from the result are inactive\" — Loom returns ALL sessions (busy AND idle), so even if the envelope were corrected, the functional semantics would still be wrong. To fix correctly, Loom needs to `filter(|s| lookup_run(...).is_some())` before mapping. Other findings: empty-string defaults for missing `modelID`/`providerID` (low), N+1 lock acquisitions (low), extra fields not in contract (low).

reviewed_deviations.reviewer_notes: CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/v2_compat.rs:102`: `Json(json!({\"sessions\": sessions}))` where `sessions` is `Vec<Value>` array of rich objects. Contract `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:147` requires `Schema.Struct({ data: Schema.Record(Session.ID, SessionActive) })`. The contract expects a JSON object keyed by SessionID; Loom emits a JSON array wrapped in `{sessions: [...]}`. These are fundamentally different wire shapes. Severity `high` correct: schema-strict clients cannot parse Loom's response at all.

CONFIRMED. Re-read `apps/server/src/handlers/v2_compat.rs:94`: `\"state\": if crate::state::lookup_run(&state, &session.id).is_some() { \"busy\" } else { \"idle\" }`. Loom uses two-value enum (busy/idle). Contract's `SessionActive = Schema.Struct({ type: Schema.Literal(\"running\") })` — single literal value. Even if the envelope were corrected to `{data: Record}`, the value shape `{state: \"busy\"|\"idle\"}` would not match `{type: \"running\"}`. Severity `medium` correct.

new_deviations_found.title: Read locks held during response construction
new_deviations_found.contract_says: No contract text on lock semantics.

The `parts` lock is explicitly dropped at line 720 (`drop(parts)`) but `messages` lock is held through the end of the function.

new_deviations_found.title: `sessionLocationMiddleware` not applied (only functionally mirrored)

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings are accurate and well-evidenced. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:686-722`, `apps/server/src/routes.rs:436-438`, and `packages/protocol/src/groups/session.ts:292-305` confirms all 9 deviations: (1) DEV-1 (items are `{info, parts}` not flat `SessionMessage.Message`) is CRITICAL — verified at lines 714-717; (2) DEV-2 (no `type` discriminator on items) is CRITICAL — verified that `MessageInfo` has no `type` field; (3) DEV-3 (single `MessageInfo` shape, not 8-variant tagged union) is HIGH — verified only `MessageInfo` exists; (4) DEV-4 (`time` is untyped `serde_json::Value`) is HIGH — verified at state.rs:326; (5) DEV-5 (extra top-level fields not in contract variants) is LOW — verified extras like `role`, `tool`, `providerID`, `modelID`, etc.; (6) DEV-6 (per-item `parts` array not in contract) is MEDIUM — verified at line 716; (7) DEV-7 (no `ses_` brand validation) is MEDIUM — verified at line 691; (8) DEV-8 (`UnknownError` (500) never returned) is MEDIUM — verified at line 715; (9) DEV-9 (`UnauthorizedError` (401) never returned) is MEDIUM — verified no auth middleware. Behavior analysis: read-only, returns immediately, no SSE events, no mutations, no auth bypass (server-wide applies), no state leakage. Concurrent reads safe (parking_lot RwLock). Found 4 new findings: (1) read locks held during response construction (low, performance); (2) stale TODO comment at routes.rs:913 (informational); (3) endpoint returns ALL messages not just post-compaction (informational, by design); (4) `sessionLocationMiddleware` not applied (medium, architectural gap). The auditor's `non_conformant` classification is correct.

output.overall_assessment: The auditor's findings (DEV-1 envelope, DEV-2 404 body) are accurate but **miss the most important schema deviations**. Independent re-reading of `apps/server/src/handlers/session.rs:55-62` (handler), `apps/server/src/state.rs:223-262` (`SessionInfo` struct), and `packages/schema/src/session.ts:19-44` (`Session.Info` contract) reveals **THREE HIGH-severity structural deviations the auditor missed**: (1) `cost: Schema.Finite` is REQUIRED by contract but Loom has `Option<f64>` with `serialize_with = \"serialize_optional\"` — field is OMITTED when `None`. (2) `tokens: Schema.Struct({...})` is REQUIRED by contract but Loom has `Option<TokensInfo>` — the whole struct is absent when `None`. (3) `location: Location.Ref = { directory, workspaceID?, project: {id, directory} }` is REQUIRED as a nested struct but Loom has flat fields `directory` + `workspaceID` at the top level — the `project` sub-struct is entirely missing. Plus extras: `slug`, `version`, `path`, `summary`, `share`, `permission`, `metadata`, flattened `extras` HashMap, `time.compacting` (low severity), and `ModelInfo` shape mismatch with contract's `Model.Ref` (low severity). The auditor's `partial` classification understates the severity — the missing required fields and missing nested `location.project` are HIGH-severity structural deviations that any v2 SDK client would fail to parse.
